column3: A written, formal word: a pet or any dog in speech is 狗, and 犬 lives on in set words such as 警犬. It began as a picture of a dog seen from the side.
column4: 警犬帮助警察找到了失踪的人。
column5: 警犬幫助警察找到了失蹤的人。
column6: Jǐng quǎn bāngzhù jǐngchá zhǎodào le shīzōng de rén.
column7: The police dog helped the police find the missing person.
column9: A written, formal word: a pet or any dog in speech is 狗, and 犬 lives on in set words such as 警犬. It began as a picture of a dog seen from the side.

column3: A literary word for a boat: in speech you say 船. It lives on in set phrases such as 同舟共济 (to pull together, as if in the same boat).
column4: 我们同舟共济，一起渡过难关。
column5: 我們同舟共濟，一起渡過難關。
column6: Wǒmen tóng zhōu gòng jì, yīqǐ dùguò nánguān.
column7: We are in this together and will get through the hard times as one.
column9: A literary word for a boat: in speech you say 船. It lives on in set phrases such as 同舟共濟 (to pull together, as if in the same boat).

column3: Praise for something you can't stop handling, such as a book, a gadget, a toy or a gift. It is said of things, not of people.
column4: 这本书太好看了，我简直爱不释手。
column5: 這本書太好看了，我簡直愛不釋手。
column6: Zhè běn shū tài hǎokàn le, wǒ jiǎnzhí àibùshìshǒu.
column7: This book is so good that I can't put it down.
column9: Praise for something you can't stop handling, such as a book, a gadget, a toy or a gift. It is said of things, not of people.

column3: Formal: the love and respect that many people feel for a leader, teacher or other admired figure, from below to above. It is not for friends or a partner, and it often turns up as 深受爱戴, 'deeply loved and respected'. In the oracle bone script, 戴 was a picture of a person holding something on their head with both hands.
column4: 这位老师深受学生的爱戴。
column5: 這位老師深受學生的愛戴。
column6: Zhè wèi lǎoshī shēnshòu xuéshēng de àidài.
column7: This teacher is deeply loved and respected by her students.
column9: Formal: the love and respect that many people feel for a leader, teacher or other admired figure, from below to above. It is not for friends or a partner, and it often turns up as 深受愛戴, 'deeply loved and respected'. In the oracle bone script, 戴 was a picture of a person holding something on their head with both hands.

column3: Most often about a relationship that is more than friendship but not official, with an undefined closeness (关系暧昧). It also fits a vague, noncommittal attitude or answer.
column4: 他们两个人的关系有点暧昧。
column5: 他們兩個人的關係有點曖昧。
column6: Tāmen liǎng gè rén de guānxi yǒudiǎn àimèi.
column7: The relationship between the two of them is a bit ambiguous.
column9: Most often about a relationship that is more than friendship but not official, with an undefined closeness (關係曖昧). It also fits a vague, noncommittal attitude or answer.

column3: Describes a place, a life or a mind that is free of disturbance, often after trouble has passed (恢复安宁). It also appears in wishes and in 不得安宁, 'get no peace'. 宁 is also read nìng, meaning 'would rather'.
column4: 战争结束后，这个小镇终于恢复了安宁。
column5: 戰爭結束後，這個小鎮終於恢復了安寧。
column6: Zhànzhēng jiéshù hòu, zhège xiǎozhèn zhōngyú huīfù le ānníng.
column7: After the war ended, the little town finally became peaceful again.
column9: Describes a place, a life or a mind that is free of disturbance, often after trouble has passed (恢復安寧). It also appears in wishes and in 不得安寧, 'get no peace'. 寧 is also read nìng, meaning 'would rather'.

column3: Describes a calm, unhurried look or manner, especially of a face, a sleeper or an elderly person. 安详地离去 is a gentle way to say someone died peacefully. For a place or a time of life, use 安宁.
column4: 老人安详地睡着了。
column5: 老人安詳地睡著了。
column6: Lǎorén ānxiáng de shuìzháo le.
column7: The old man fell peacefully asleep.
column9: Describes a calm, unhurried look or manner, especially of a face, a sleeper or an elderly person. 安詳地離去 is a gentle way to say someone died peacefully. For a place or a time of life, use 安寧.

column3: A case in the legal or police sense, one that is investigated, tried or solved (侦破案件, 审理案件). It is counted with 起: 一起案件. For a case used as an illustration, see 案例.
column4: 警方已经侦破了这起案件。
column5: 警方已經偵破了這起案件。
column6: Jǐngfāng yǐjīng zhēnpò le zhè qǐ ànjiàn.
column7: The police have already solved this case.
column9: A case in the legal or police sense, one that is investigated, tried or solved (偵破案件, 審理案件). It is counted with 起: 一起案件. For a case used as an illustration, see 案例.

column3: A concrete case used to illustrate a point in teaching, business, law or medicine (典型案例, 成功案例, 分析案例). Unlike 案件, it need not be a legal case being handled.
column4: 这本书里有很多真实的案例。
column5: 這本書裡有很多真實的案例。
column6: Zhè běn shū lǐ yǒu hěn duō zhēnshí de ànlì.
column7: This book has many real case studies.
column9: A concrete case used to illustrate a point in teaching, business, law or medicine (典型案例, 成功案例, 分析案例). Unlike 案件, it need not be a legal case being handled.

column3: A more formal word than 贵, used for goods, fees and costs. It is also used in figures of speech, as in 昂贵的代价, 'a heavy price'.
column4: 这块手表非常昂贵。
column5: 這塊手錶非常昂貴。
column6: Zhè kuài shǒubiǎo fēicháng ángguì.
column7: This watch is very expensive.
column9: A more formal word than 貴, used for goods, fees and costs. It is also used in figures of speech, as in 昂貴的代價, 'a heavy price'.

column3: Usually seen in the set phrase 凹凸不平, 'bumpy', for a road, a wall or skin. The two characters are opposites: 凹 for the hollows and 凸 for the bumps. Taiwan reads 凸 as tú.
column4: 这条路凹凸不平，骑车要小心。
column5: 這條路凹凸不平，騎車要小心。
column6: Zhè tiáo lù āotū bùpíng, qí chē yào xiǎoxīn.
column7: This road is bumpy, so be careful when you bike.
column9: Usually seen in the set phrase 凹凸不平, 'bumpy', for a road, a wall or skin. The two characters are opposites: 凹 for the hollows and 凸 for the bumps. Taiwan reads 凸 as tú.

column3: A deep secret of nature, the universe, life or a field of knowledge that is still being worked out (探索宇宙的奥秘). It is not a secret someone keeps from you: that is 秘密.
column4: 科学家一直在探索宇宙的奥秘。
column5: 科學家一直在探索宇宙的奧祕。
column6: Kēxuéjiā yīzhí zài tànsuǒ yǔzhòu de àomì.
column7: Scientists have always been exploring the mysteries of the universe.
column9: A deep secret of nature, the universe, life or a field of knowledge that is still being worked out (探索宇宙的奧祕). It is not a secret someone keeps from you: that is 秘密.

column3: Spoken. It is followed by a verb or a clause that states what the speaker wishes for (巴不得马上放假). The wish is often for something that can't happen yet, or not so soon. 巴 on its own can mean to long for or to cling to.
column4: 我巴不得明天就放假。
column5: 我巴不得明天就放假。
column6: Wǒ bābude míngtiān jiù fàngjià.
column7: I wish vacation would start tomorrow.
column9: Spoken. It is followed by a verb or a clause that states what the speaker wishes for (巴不得馬上放假). The wish is often for something that can't happen yet, or not so soon. 巴 on its own can mean to long for or to cling to.

column3: Critical: it describes someone who flatters or does favors for a boss or other powerful person to gain something (巴结老板). Nobody describes themselves this way.
column4: 他总是巴结老板，同事都不喜欢他。
column5: 他總是巴結老闆，同事都不喜歡他。
column6: Tā zǒngshì bājie lǎobǎn, tóngshì dōu bù xǐhuan tā.
column7: He is always sucking up to the boss, and his coworkers don't like him.
column9: Critical: it describes someone who flatters or does favors for a boss or other powerful person to gain something (巴結老闆). Nobody describes themselves this way.

column3: Done with the hands, often with force, and usually followed by a result or direction word: 扒开 (pull apart), 扒下来 (pull off), 扒着 (hang on to), 扒皮 (skin). 扒 is also read pá, meaning to steal.
column4: 小孩扒着栏杆往外看。
column5: 小孩扒著欄杆往外看。
column6: Xiǎohái bā zhe lángān wǎng wài kàn.
column7: The child clung to the railing and looked outside.
column9: Done with the hands, often with force, and usually followed by a result or direction word: 扒開 (pull apart), 扒下來 (pull off), 扒著 (hang on to), 扒皮 (skin). 扒 is also read pá, meaning to steal.

column3: The mark left on skin after a wound has healed, or a blemish on an object. The usual compounds are 伤疤 and 刀疤. 揭伤疤 means to reopen an old wound, figuratively.
column4: 他脸上有一道长长的疤。
column5: 他臉上有一道長長的疤。
column6: Tā liǎn shang yǒu yī dào chángcháng de bā.
column7: He has a long scar on his face.
column9: The mark left on skin after a wound has healed, or a blemish on an object. The usual compounds are 傷疤 and 刀疤. 揭傷疤 means to reopen an old wound, figuratively.

column3: Criticism of rushing something and ruining it, especially children's education or a project that needs time. It comes from a story in Mencius about a farmer who pulled his seedlings up to help them grow, and killed them.
column4: 学习要循序渐进，不能拔苗助长。
column5: 學習要循序漸進，不能拔苗助長。
column6: Xuéxí yào xúnxù jiànjìn, bù néng bámiáozhùzhǎng.
column7: Study should go step by step; you can't force it.
column9: Criticism of rushing something and ruining it, especially children's education or a project that needs time. It comes from a story in Mencius about a farmer who pulled his seedlings up to help them grow, and killed them.

column3: In everyday use it means to be the gatekeeper who checks quality or standards before something goes through: 严格把关, 为质量把关.
column4: 他负责为每一份报告把关。
column5: 他負責為每一份報告把關。
column6: Tā fùzé wèi měi yī fèn bàogào bǎguān.
column7: He is responsible for checking every report.
column9: In everyday use it means to be the gatekeeper who checks quality or standards before something goes through: 嚴格把關, 為質量把關.

column3: The part you grip on a door, a cup, a drawer or a tool: 门把手 is a door handle. A stair railing is a 扶手 instead. 把 is also the measure word for things with a handle.
column4: 这个杯子的把手断了。
column5: 這個杯子的把手斷了。
column6: Zhège bēizi de bǎshou duàn le.
column7: The handle of this cup has broken off.
column9: The part you grip on a door, a cup, a drawer or a tool: 門把手 is a door handle. A stair railing is a 扶手 instead. 把 is also the measure word for things with a handle.

column3: Describes a person or behavior that is overbearing and pushes others around. It is also used of strong medicine or liquor. 霸道总裁, the domineering boss, is a favorite figure in romance stories.
column4: 他说话很霸道，从不听别人的话。
column5: 他說話很霸道，從不聽別人的話。
column6: Tā shuōhuà hěn bàdào, cóng bù tīng biérén de huà.
column7: He talks in a domineering way and never listens to anyone.
column9: Describes a person or behavior that is overbearing and pushes others around. It is also used of strong medicine or liquor. 霸道總裁, the domineering boss, is a favorite figure in romance stories.

column3: Colloquial, done with the hands: 掰开 a piece of bread, 掰玉米 off the cob. It also turns up in 瞎掰, 'to make things up'.
column4: 他把面包掰成两半。
column5: 他把麵包掰成兩半。
column6: Tā bǎ miànbāo bāi chéng liǎng bàn.
column7: He broke the bread in two.
column9: Colloquial, done with the hands: 掰開 a piece of bread, 掰玉米 off the cob. It also turns up in 瞎掰, 'to make things up'.

column3: Used for abstract things, such as 败坏名声 (ruin a reputation), 败坏风气 (corrupt public customs) and 道德败坏 (morally corrupt). A physical object that breaks is just 坏.
column4: 这种行为败坏了公司的名声。
column5: 這種行為敗壞了公司的名聲。
column6: Zhè zhǒng xíngwéi bàihuài le gōngsī de míngshēng.
column7: This kind of behavior has ruined the company's reputation.
column9: Used for abstract things, such as 敗壞名聲 (ruin a reputation), 敗壞風氣 (corrupt public customs) and 道德敗壞 (morally corrupt). A physical object that breaks is just 壞.

column3: Formal, in news and official writing: a government or authority issues a law, regulation or order (颁布法令, 颁布条例). For prizes and certificates, use 颁发. The 布 is the 'announce' of 宣布 and 公布, not cloth.
column4: 政府颁布了新的环保法规。
column5: 政府頒布了新的環保法規。
column6: Zhèngfǔ bānbù le xīn de huánbǎo fǎguī.
column7: The government issued new environmental regulations.
column9: Formal, in news and official writing: a government or authority issues a law, regulation or order (頒布法令, 頒布條例). For prizes and certificates, use 頒發. The 布 is the 'announce' of 宣布 and 公布, not cloth.

column3: Used for an official handing out of prizes, diplomas, certificates and licenses (颁发证书, 颁发奖状), as at a ceremony. For laws and regulations, use 颁布.
column4: 校长给优秀的学生颁发了奖状。
column5: 校長給優秀的學生頒發了獎狀。
column6: Xiàozhǎng gěi yōuxiù de xuéshēng bānfā le jiǎngzhuàng.
column7: The principal presented certificates to the outstanding students.
column9: Used for an official handing out of prizes, diplomas, certificates and licenses (頒發證書, 頒發獎狀), as at a ceremony. For laws and regulations, use 頒布.

column3: Mostly a bound character in compounds: 斑点 (spots), 斑纹 (stripes), 雀斑 (freckles), 老年斑 (age spots), 斑马 (zebra).
column4: 这只猫身上有一块黑斑。
column5: 這隻貓身上有一塊黑斑。
column6: Zhè zhī māo shēn shang yǒu yī kuài hēi bān.
column7: This cat has a black patch on its body.
column9: Mostly a bound character in compounds: 斑點 (spots), 斑紋 (stripes), 雀斑 (freckles), 老年斑 (age spots), 斑馬 (zebra).

column3: Covers software releases (更新到最新版本) as well as editions of books, cuts of a film and different tellings of a story. The number is the 版本号.
column4: 请把手机系统更新到最新版本。
column5: 請把手機系統更新到最新版本。
column6: Qǐng bǎ shǒujī xìtǒng gēngxīn dào zuìxīn bǎnběn.
column7: Please update your phone's system to the latest version.
column9: Covers software releases (更新到最新版本) as well as editions of books, cuts of a film and different tellings of a story. The number is the 版本號.

column3: Said as criticism or as a warning about study, exercise, diets or projects: 做事不能半途而废. It is common in both speech and writing.
column4: 学习不能半途而废，要坚持到底。
column5: 學習不能半途而廢，要堅持到底。
column6: Xuéxí bù néng bàntú'érfèi, yào jiānchí dàodǐ.
column7: You can't give up halfway through studying; you must see it through.
column9: Said as criticism or as a warning about study, exercise, diets or projects: 做事不能半途而廢. It is common in both speech and writing.

column3: Most often a life partner: a spouse or long-term lover, in a fairly formal tone. For a companion on a trip or in an activity, 同伴 is the usual word.
column4: 他们是一对幸福的伴侣。
column5: 他們是一對幸福的伴侶。
column6: Tāmen shì yī duì xìngfú de bànlǚ.
column7: They are a happy couple.
column9: Most often a life partner: a spouse or long-term lover, in a fairly formal tone. For a companion on a trip or in an activity, 同伴 is the usual word.

column3: Mostly for things that come along with something else, such as a symptom, a feeling or a side effect, usually in the pattern 伴随着. It is less natural for a person walking with you; use 陪 for that.
column4: 疼痛常常伴随发烧出现。
column5: 疼痛常常伴隨發燒出現。
column6: Téngtòng chángcháng bànsuí fāshāo chūxiàn.
column7: Pain often appears together with a fever.
column9: Mostly for things that come along with something else, such as a symptom, a feeling or a side effect, usually in the pattern 伴隨著. It is less natural for a person walking with you; use 陪 for that.

column3: Kidnapping a person. It is also used figuratively: 道德绑架 is pressuring someone with moral demands until they give in.
column4: 警方成功救出了被绑架的孩子。
column5: 警方成功救出了被綁架的孩子。
column6: Jǐngfāng chénggōng jiùchū le bèi bǎngjià de háizi.
column7: The police rescued the kidnapped child.
column9: Kidnapping a person. It is also used figuratively: 道德綁架 is pressuring someone with moral demands until they give in.

column3: Always for covering up for someone who did wrong, such as a criminal or a corrupt colleague, so it is a charge, not praise. Neutral protection is 保护. The 广 in 庇 is a shelter built against a cliff.
column4: 他因包庇罪犯被判了刑。
column5: 他因包庇罪犯被判了刑。
column6: Tā yīn bāobì zuìfàn bèi pàn le xíng.
column7: He was sentenced for harboring a criminal.
column9: Always for covering up for someone who did wrong, such as a criminal or a corrupt colleague, so it is a charge, not praise. Neutral protection is 保護. The 广 in 庇 is a shelter built against a cliff.

column3: Besides the cloth bundle itself, it is a burden you carry in your mind: 思想包袱, 心理包袱. In comedy, 抖包袱 is delivering the punchline.
column4: 别给自己太大的心理包袱。
column5: 別給自己太大的心理包袱。
column6: Bié gěi zìjǐ tài dà de xīnlǐ bāofu.
column7: Don't put too much mental pressure on yourself.
column9: Besides the cloth bundle itself, it is a burden you carry in your mind: 思想包袱, 心理包袱. In comedy, 抖包袱 is delivering the punchline.

column3: A technical word for a solution that can hold no more, and by extension a market or city that has reached its limit: 市场饱和. Being full from food is just 饱.
column4: 这个城市的市场已经饱和了。
column5: 這個城市的市場已經飽和了。
column6: Zhège chéngshì de shìchǎng yǐjīng bǎohé le.
column7: This city's market is already saturated.
column9: A technical word for a solution that can hold no more, and by extension a market or city that has reached its limit: 市場飽和. Being full from food is just 飽.

column3: Written, respectful or sympathetic: it describes an older person, or a place, whose face and manner show a long life of hardship and change, usually as 饱经沧桑的 plus a noun such as 脸 or 老人. 沧桑 is short for 沧海桑田, "the blue sea turned into mulberry fields": great changes.
column4: 这位饱经沧桑的老人讲起了往事。
column5: 這位飽經滄桑的老人講起了往事。
column6: Zhè wèi bǎojīngcāngsāng de lǎorén jiǎng qǐ le wǎngshì.
column7: This man, who has lived through so much, began to tell of the past.
column9: Written, respectful or sympathetic: it describes an older person, or a place, whose face and manner show a long life of hardship and change, usually as 飽經滄桑的 plus a noun such as 臉 or 老人. 滄桑 is short for 滄海桑田, "the blue sea turned into mulberry fields": great changes.

column3: As a verb, to keep something safe for its owner: 保管行李, 请妥善保管. In speech it can also be a promise, as in 保管你满意, "I guarantee you will be satisfied."
column4: 请把贵重物品交给我保管。
column5: 請把貴重物品交給我保管。
column6: Qǐng bǎ guìzhòng wùpǐn jiāo gěi wǒ bǎoguǎn.
column7: Please leave your valuables with me for safekeeping.
column9: As a verb, to keep something safe for its owner: 保管行李, 請妥善保管. In speech it can also be a promise, as in 保管你滿意, "I guarantee you will be satisfied."

column3: A paid helper who looks after children and often the home. On the mainland she is politely called 阿姨, and a nanny for a newborn's first month is a 月嫂.
column4: 他们请了一位保姆照顾孩子。
column5: 他們請了一位保姆照顧孩子。
column6: Tāmen qǐng le yī wèi bǎomǔ zhàogù háizi.
column7: They hired a nanny to look after the child.
column9: A paid helper who looks after children and often the home. On the mainland she is politely called 阿姨, and a nanny for a newborn's first month is a 月嫂.

column3: Said to someone else when parting or at the end of a letter, wishing them good health: 多保重, 请保重身体. You don't say it about yourself, and it is warmer than a plain goodbye.
column4: 天气冷了，你要多保重。
column5: 天氣冷了，你要多保重。
column6: Tiānqì lěng le, nǐ yào duō bǎozhòng.
column7: It's getting cold, so take good care of yourself.
column9: Said to someone else when parting or at the end of a letter, wishing them good health: 多保重, 請保重身體. You don't say it about yourself, and it is warmer than a plain goodbye.

column3: Pay for work or a favor, a little more formal than 工资 and wider: it covers fees and non-money rewards. Typical phrases are 获得报酬 and 没有报酬.
column4: 这份工作的报酬很高。
column5: 這份工作的報酬很高。
column6: Zhè fèn gōngzuò de bàochou hěn gāo.
column7: The pay for this job is very high.
column9: Pay for work or a favor, a little more formal than 工資 and wider: it covers fees and non-money rewards. Typical phrases are 獲得報酬 and 沒有報酬.

column3: Hitting back at someone who harmed you, with a bitter, negative tone: 报复他, 遭到报复. For revenge on a big wrong, as in stories, 复仇 is the dramatic word.
column4: 他担心老板会报复他。
column5: 他擔心老闆會報復他。
column6: Tā dānxīn lǎobǎn huì bàofù tā.
column7: He worries that the boss will get back at him.
column9: Hitting back at someone who harmed you, with a bitter, negative tone: 報復他, 遭到報復. For revenge on a big wrong, as in stories, 復仇 is the dramatic word.

column3: What you do with receipts: claim back work expenses, as in 发票报销 or 差旅费报销. In speech it also means written off, said of something broken beyond repair: 手机掉水里，报销了.
column4: 出差的费用公司可以报销。
column5: 出差的費用公司可以報銷。
column6: Chūchāi de fèiyong gōngsī kěyǐ bàoxiāo.
column7: The company can reimburse the costs of a business trip.
column9: What you do with receipts: claim back work expenses, as in 發票報銷 or 差旅費報銷. In speech it also means written off, said of something broken beyond repair: 手機掉水裡，報銷了.

column3: A big, positive aim in life, never a small plan: 有抱负 describes a person, and 实现抱负 means to live out one's ideals.
column4: 他是一个有抱负的年轻人。
column5: 他是一個有抱負的年輕人。
column6: Tā shì yī gè yǒu bàofù de niánqīngrén.
column7: He is an ambitious young man.
column9: A big, positive aim in life, never a small plan: 有抱負 describes a person, and 實現抱負 means to live out one's ideals.

column3: Exposure in photography, and figuratively a secret or scandal coming out: 被曝光, 曝光丑闻. It also describes how much attention something gets, as in advertising. Taiwan reads the first character pù.
column4: 这件丑闻昨天被媒体曝光了。
column5: 這件醜聞昨天被媒體曝光了。
column6: Zhè jiàn chǒuwén zuótiān bèi méitǐ bàoguāng le.
column7: The media exposed this scandal yesterday.
column9: Exposure in photography, and figuratively a secret or scandal coming out: 被曝光, 曝光醜聞. It also describes how much attention something gets, as in advertising. Taiwan reads the first character pù.

column3: A strong insult for dishonest, underhanded people or behavior: 卑鄙小人, 卑鄙的手段. It is about moral character, not low social rank. 卑 began as a man holding a fan, a servant, and 鄙 as a border town; today 鄙 means rustic, low.
column4: 他用卑鄙的手段抢走了我的客户。
column5: 他用卑鄙的手段搶走了我的客戶。
column6: Tā yòng bēibǐ de shǒuduàn qiǎngzǒu le wǒ de kèhù.
column7: He used a dirty trick to steal my client.
column9: A strong insult for dishonest, underhanded people or behavior: 卑鄙小人, 卑鄙的手段. It is about moral character, not low social rank. 卑 began as a man holding a fan, a servant, and 鄙 as a border town; today 鄙 means rustic, low.

column3: A heavy, deep sadness, heavier than 难过, and also a verdict on a sorry state of affairs: 这是时代的悲哀, "this is the tragedy of our times."
column4: 他为自己的失败感到悲哀。
column5: 他為自己的失敗感到悲哀。
column6: Tā wèi zìjǐ de shībài gǎndào bēi'āi.
column7: He felt sorrow over his own failure.
column9: A heavy, deep sadness, heavier than 難過, and also a verdict on a sorry state of affairs: 這是時代的悲哀, "this is the tragedy of our times."

column3: 贝 began as a picture of a cowrie shell, which served as money in ancient China.
column4: 孩子们在海边捡了很多贝壳。
column5: 孩子們在海邊撿了很多貝殼。
column6: Háizimen zài hǎibiān jiǎn le hěn duō bèiké.
column7: The children picked up lots of shells at the beach.
column9: 貝 began as a picture of a cowrie shell, which served as money in ancient China.

column3: Mostly about data: it is both a verb ("back up") and a noun ("a backup"), as in 做备份. For a spare key or a spare plan the word is 备用: 备用钥匙.
column4: 手机里的照片要记得备份。
column5: 手機裡的照片要記得備份。
column6: Shǒujī lǐ de zhàopiàn yào jìde bèifèn.
column7: Remember to back up the photos on your phone.
column9: Mostly about data: it is both a verb ("back up") and a noun ("a backup"), as in 做備份. For a spare key or a spare plan the word is 備用: 備用鑰匙.

column3: A small record to jog your memory, now also the name of the notes app on many phones. In diplomacy it is a formal memorandum.
column4: 我把会议时间记在手机备忘录里了。
column5: 我把會議時間記在手機備忘錄裡了。
column6: Wǒ bǎ huìyì shíjiān jì zài shǒujī bèiwànglù lǐ le.
column7: I wrote the meeting time in my phone's notes app.
column9: A small record to jog your memory, now also the name of the notes app on many phones. In diplomacy it is a formal memorandum.

column3: Betraying trust: a friend, a spouse, a promise or one's country. Defecting to the other side is 叛变, and rebelling against authority is 反叛.
column4: 他背叛了多年的朋友。
column5: 他背叛了多年的朋友。
column6: Tā bèipàn le duōnián de péngyou.
column7: He betrayed a friend of many years.
column9: Betraying trust: a friend, a spouse, a promise or one's country. Defecting to the other side is 叛變, and rebelling against authority is 反叛.

column3: The school word for reciting from memory: poems, texts, passages. Unlike 朗读, reading aloud, you do it without looking at the page. Here 背 is read bèi, but it is bēi when it means to carry on one's back.
column4: 老师要求我们背诵这首古诗。
column5: 老師要求我們背誦這首古詩。
column6: Lǎoshī yāoqiú wǒmen bèisòng zhè shǒu gǔshī.
column7: The teacher asked us to recite this old poem.
column9: The school word for reciting from memory: poems, texts, passages. Unlike 朗讀, reading aloud, you do it without looking at the page. Here 背 is read bèi, but it is bēi when it means to carry on one's back.

column3: Wearing yourself out by constantly traveling or running around, usually for a living or a cause: 为生活奔波, 奔波劳碌. The tiredness is part of the feeling.
column4: 他为了生活四处奔波。
column5: 他為了生活四處奔波。
column6: Tā wèile shēnghuó sìchù bēnbō.
column7: He runs around everywhere to make a living.
column9: Wearing yourself out by constantly traveling or running around, usually for a living or a cause: 為生活奔波, 奔波勞碌. The tiredness is part of the feeling.

column3: A vivid, written word for horses, trains or cars racing along. It is also the mainland name of Mercedes-Benz; Taiwan says 宾士.
column4: 骏马在草原奔驰。
column5: 駿馬在草原奔馳。
column6: Jùnmǎ zài cǎoyuán bēnchí.
column7: Fine horses gallop across the grassland.
column9: A vivid, written word for horses, trains or cars racing along. It is also the mainland name of Mercedes-Benz; Taiwan says 賓士.

column3: Behavior you are born with, not taught: 本能反应, 出于本能, 求生本能. 本 shows a tree with a stroke marking its roots, which fits an ability you have from the start.
column4: 婴儿天生就有吸吮的本能。
column5: 嬰兒天生就有吸吮的本能。
column6: Yīng'ér tiānshēng jiù yǒu xīshǔn de běnnéng.
column7: Babies are born with the instinct to suck.
column9: Behavior you are born with, not taught: 本能反應, 出於本能, 求生本能. 本 shows a tree with a stroke marking its roots, which fits an ability you have from the start.

column3: Beyond money to start a business, it is the everyday word for whatever you can build on or afford to gamble with: youth, health, talent, looks.
column4: 你有这么好的身体，就是最大的本钱。
column5: 你有這麼好的身體，就是最大的本錢。
column6: Nǐ yǒu zhème hǎo de shēntǐ, jiù shì zuì dà de běnqián.
column7: With a body this healthy, you already have your biggest asset.
column9: Beyond money to start a business, it is the everyday word for whatever you can build on or afford to gamble with: youth, health, talent, looks.

column3: Softer than 笨 alone: it describes clumsy movements, hands or speech (动作笨拙, 笨拙的表达) and a lack of skill rather than low intelligence. Taiwan reads 拙 as zhuó, with the second tone.
column4: 他第一次做饭，动作很笨拙。
column5: 他第一次做飯，動作很笨拙。
column6: Tā dì yī cì zuò fàn, dòngzuò hěn bènzhuō.
column7: It was his first time cooking, and his movements were very clumsy.
column9: Softer than 笨 alone: it describes clumsy movements, hands or speech (動作笨拙, 笨拙的表達) and a lack of skill rather than low intelligence. Taiwan reads 拙 as zhuó, with the second tone.

column3: Used for systems, economies and defenses, and for a person's emotional state (情绪崩溃). In casual speech 我崩溃了 means I can't take it anymore. 崩 is the word for a mountain giving way, and 溃 for floodwaters breaking through a dam or an army being routed.
column4: 他听到消息后情绪崩溃了。
column5: 他聽到消息後情緒崩潰了。
column6: Tā tīngdào xiāoxi hòu qíngxù bēngkuì le.
column7: After hearing the news, he broke down emotionally.
column9: Used for systems, economies and defenses, and for a person's emotional state (情緒崩潰). In casual speech 我崩潰了 means I can't take it anymore. 崩 is the word for a mountain giving way, and 潰 for floodwaters breaking through a dam or an army being routed.

column3: A spoken word that goes before a verb to wave something off: 甭客气, 甭说了. In writing and formal speech it is 不用. It comes from a northern dialect's way of pronouncing 不用.
column4: 你甭担心，我来处理。
column5: 你甭擔心，我來處理。
column6: Nǐ béng dānxīn, wǒ lái chǔlǐ.
column7: No need to worry, I'll handle it.
column9: A spoken word that goes before a verb to wave something off: 甭客氣, 甭說了. In writing and formal speech it is 不用. It comes from a northern dialect's way of pronouncing 不用.

column3: Said of something sudden and strong coming out: sparks, laughter, applause, passion or talent. A common pattern is 迸发出 plus a noun (迸发出热情).
column4: 观众席上迸发出热烈的掌声。
column5: 觀眾席上迸發出熱烈的掌聲。
column6: Guānzhòngxí shàng bèngfā chū rèliè de zhǎngshēng.
column7: Warm applause burst out from the audience.
column9: Said of something sudden and strong coming out: sparks, laughter, applause, passion or talent. A common pattern is 迸發出 plus a noun (迸發出熱情).

column3: A lively spoken word for jumping up and down or hopping with both feet (蹦蹦跳跳). It also appears in 蹦极 for bungee jumping and 蹦迪 for dancing at a club.
column4: 孩子们高兴得蹦了起来。
column5: 孩子們高興得蹦了起來。
column6: Háizimen gāoxìng de bèng le qǐlái.
column7: The children were so happy they jumped up and down.
column9: A lively spoken word for jumping up and down or hopping with both feet (蹦蹦跳跳). It also appears in 蹦極 for bungee jumping and 蹦迪 for dancing at a club.

column3: Stronger and more formal than 逼 alone. The pattern is 逼迫某人做某事, and it is often passive (被逼迫) when circumstances or other people leave no choice.
column4: 没有人逼迫你做这件事。
column5: 沒有人逼迫你做這件事。
column6: Méiyǒu rén bīpò nǐ zuò zhè jiàn shì.
column7: Nobody is forcing you to do this.
column9: Stronger and more formal than 逼 alone. The pattern is 逼迫某人做某事, and it is often passive (被逼迫) when circumstances or other people leave no choice.

column3: As a verb it fits 用A来比喻B or 把A比喻成B; as a noun it is a figure of speech. In casual speech people say 打比方 instead.
column4: 人们常用春蚕来比喻老师。
column5: 人們常用春蠶來比喻老師。
column6: Rénmen cháng yòng chūncán lái bǐyù lǎoshī.
column7: People often use the spring silkworm as a metaphor for teachers.
column9: As a verb it fits 用A來比喻B or 把A比喻成B; as a noun it is a figure of speech. In casual speech people say 打比方 instead.

column3: Stronger than 看不起: open contempt, usually for someone's character or conduct. It is common in the passive (被鄙视) and in the online word 鄙视链, a ranking of who looks down on whom. On its own 鄙 means base or vulgar, as in 卑鄙.
column4: 我很鄙视那些说谎的人。
column5: 我很鄙視那些說謊的人。
column6: Wǒ hěn bǐshì nàxiē shuōhuǎng de rén.
column7: I really look down on people who lie.
column9: Stronger than 看不起: open contempt, usually for someone's character or conduct. It is common in the passive (被鄙視) and in the online word 鄙視鏈, a ranking of who looks down on whom. On its own 鄙 means base or vulgar, as in 卑鄙.

column3: Describes places that are hard to reach (交通闭塞, a remote village) and people or areas cut off from news and new ideas (消息闭塞, 思想闭塞). The 塞 here is read sè, the sense of blocking, not sāi, as in stuffing something in.
column4: 那个村子交通闭塞，很少有人去过。
column5: 那個村子交通閉塞，很少有人去過。
column6: Nàge cūnzi jiāotōng bìsè, hěn shǎo yǒu rén qù guo.
column7: That village is hard to get to, and few people have been there.
column9: Describes places that are hard to reach (交通閉塞, a remote village) and people or areas cut off from news and new ideas (消息閉塞, 思想閉塞). The 塞 here is read sè, the sense of blocking, not sāi, as in stuffing something in.

column3: A flaw in a method, system or way of doing things, not a physical illness. It goes with 存在 and 有, and with 克服 or 消除 when it is fixed.
column4: 这种做法有很多弊病。
column5: 這種做法有很多弊病。
column6: Zhè zhǒng zuòfǎ yǒu hěn duō bìbìng.
column7: This way of doing things has many flaws.
column9: A flaw in a method, system or way of doing things, not a physical illness. It goes with 存在 and 有, and with 克服 or 消除 when it is fixed.

column3: Formal, found in news and policy writing: what is wrong with a system or rule (制度的弊端), going with 暴露, 克服 and 消除. 弊病 is the plainer word for a flaw.
column4: 这项制度的弊端已经越来越明显。
column5: 這項制度的弊端已經越來越明顯。
column6: Zhè xiàng zhìdù de bìduān yǐjīng yuèláiyuè míngxiǎn.
column7: The drawbacks of this system are becoming more and more obvious.
column9: Formal, found in news and policy writing: what is wrong with a system or rule (制度的弊端), going with 暴露, 克服 and 消除. 弊病 is the plainer word for a flaw.

column3: In speech the arm is usually 手臂. By itself 臂 stays in set phrases such as 助一臂之力 (to lend a hand) and in words like 臂膀 and 机械臂.
column4: 他有一副强壮的臂膀。
column5: 他有一副強壯的臂膀。
column6: Tā yǒu yī fù qiángzhuàng de bì bǎng.
column7: He has a pair of strong arms.
column9: In speech the arm is usually 手臂. By itself 臂 stays in set phrases such as 助一臂之力 (to lend a hand) and in words like 臂膀 and 機械臂.

column3: The far regions of a country, away from its center, with a feel of remoteness (边疆地区, 支援边疆). 边界 is the line itself, while 边疆 is the whole area near it.
column4: 他年轻时去边疆工作了十年。
column5: 他年輕時去邊疆工作了十年。
column6: Tā niánqīng shí qù biānjiāng gōngzuò le shí nián.
column7: When he was young, he worked in the frontier region for ten years.
column9: The far regions of a country, away from its center, with a feel of remoteness (邊疆地區, 支援邊疆). 邊界 is the line itself, while 邊疆 is the whole area near it.

column3: Besides the line between countries or regions, it is used for limits that are not on any map, such as the limits of a field of study or a moral limit (道德的边界).
column4: 这条河是两国的边界。
column5: 這條河是兩國的邊界。
column6: Zhè tiáo hé shì liǎng guó de biānjiè.
column7: This river is the border between the two countries.
column9: Besides the line between countries or regions, it is used for limits that are not on any map, such as the limits of a field of study or a moral limit (道德的邊界).

column3: Used for handwork with threads or strips: sweaters, baskets, nets, mats. Figuratively it means building up something hoped for or made up (编织梦想, 编织谎言).
column4: 奶奶正在编织一件毛衣。
column5: 奶奶正在編織一件毛衣。
column6: Nǎinai zhèngzài biānzhī yī jiàn máoyī.
column7: Grandma is knitting a sweater.
column9: Used for handwork with threads or strips: sweaters, baskets, nets, mats. Figuratively it means building up something hoped for or made up (編織夢想, 編織謊言).

column3: Written and fairly formal, with a positive tone: a person, a saying or a goal that pushes you to try harder. Often reflexive (自我鞭策, 鞭策自己). Both characters have to do with whipping: 鞭 is the whip itself, and 策 can mean to whip a horse.
column4: 老师的话时刻鞭策着我努力学习。
column5: 老師的話時刻鞭策著我努力學習。
column6: Lǎoshī de huà shíkè biāncè zhe wǒ nǔlì xuéxí.
column7: My teacher's words keep spurring me to study hard.
column9: Written and fairly formal, with a positive tone: a person, a saying or a goal that pushes you to try harder. Often reflexive (自我鞭策, 鞭策自己). Both characters have to do with whipping: 鞭 is the whip itself, and 策 can mean to whip a horse.

column3: The object is a person, an ability or an achievement, and the one doing it is usually unfair or unkind, often to raise themselves (贬低别人, 自我贬低).
column4: 他总是贬低别人来抬高自己。
column5: 他總是貶低別人來抬高自己。
column6: Tā zǒngshì biǎndī biéren lái táigāo zìjǐ.
column7: He always puts other people down to build himself up.
column9: The object is a person, an ability or an achievement, and the one doing it is usually unfair or unkind, often to raise themselves (貶低別人, 自我貶低).

column3: A grammar and vocabulary term: a word that carries disapproval is a 贬义词, and 褒义 is the opposite. It appears in 带有贬义 or 含贬义.
column4: 这个词带有贬义，最好别用。
column5: 這個詞帶有貶義，最好別用。
column6: Zhège cí dàiyǒu biǎnyì, zuìhǎo bié yòng.
column7: This word has a negative tone, so it is best not to use it.
column9: A grammar and vocabulary term: a word that carries disapproval is a 貶義詞, and 褒義 is the opposite. It appears in 帶有貶義 or 含貶義.

column3: A discreet word for a serious blow in someone's life, such as a death, illness or financial collapse, without saying which. The usual pattern is 发生变故 or 突遭变故.
column4: 他家里突然发生变故，不得不退学。
column5: 他家裡突然發生變故，不得不退學。
column6: Tā jiālǐ túrán fāshēng biàngù, bùdébù tuìxué.
column7: Something terrible suddenly happened in his family, and he had to drop out of school.
column9: A discreet word for a serious blow in someone's life, such as a death, illness or financial collapse, without saying which. The usual pattern is 發生變故 or 突遭變故.

column3: Large changes that unfold over a long time, in a society, a city or an era (社会变迁, 历史变迁). For everyday or sudden changes use 变化.
column4: 这座城市几十年来的变迁很大。
column5: 這座城市幾十年來的變遷很大。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì jǐshí nián lái de biànqiān hěn dà.
column7: This city has changed a great deal over the past few decades.
column9: Large changes that unfold over a long time, in a society, a city or an era (社會變遷, 歷史變遷). For everyday or sudden changes use 變化.

column3: Typical for milk, medicine and other stored goods that have spoiled (牛奶变质了). It is also used for a person, group or relationship whose nature has turned for the worse. Taiwan reads 质 as zhí here.
column4: 牛奶放太久，已经变质了。
column5: 牛奶放太久，已經變質了。
column6: Niúnǎi fàng tài jiǔ, yǐjīng biànzhì le.
column7: The milk has been left out too long and has gone bad.
column9: Typical for milk, medicine and other stored goods that have spoiled (牛奶變質了). It is also used for a person, group or relationship whose nature has turned for the worse. Taiwan reads 質 as zhí here.

column3: The subject is what spreads, and the object a place: 遍布全国, 遍布世界各地. Typical for shops, branches, fans or traces found throughout an area. 布 is cloth, but also means to spread, as in 分布 and 公布.
column4: 他们的连锁店遍布全国。
column5: 他們的連鎖店遍布全國。
column6: Tāmen de liánsuǒdiàn biànbù quánguó.
column7: Their chain stores are found all over the country.
column9: The subject is what spreads, and the object a place: 遍布全國, 遍布世界各地. Typical for shops, branches, fans or traces found throughout an area. 布 is cloth, but also means to spread, as in 分佈 and 公布.

column3: Used when something is hard to make out at first: handwriting, a face in a photo, a direction. Often with 出 or 不出 (辨认不出), and in the negative (无法辨认).
column4: 照片太模糊，我辨认不出他是谁。
column5: 照片太模糊，我辨認不出他是誰。
column6: Zhàopiàn tài móhu, wǒ biànrèn bù chū tā shì shéi.
column7: The photo is too blurry for me to tell who he is.
column9: Used when something is hard to make out at first: handwriting, a face in a photo, a direction. Often with 出 or 不出 (辨認不出), and in the negative (無法辨認).

column3: Used both in court, where a defense lawyer speaks for the accused, and in everyday arguments when you stand up for a person or a view. The pattern is 为…辩护.
column4: 他请了一位律师为自己辩护。
column5: 他請了一位律師為自己辯護。
column6: Tā qǐng le yī wèi lǜshī wèi zìjǐ biànhù.
column7: He hired a lawyer to defend him.
column9: Used both in court, where a defense lawyer speaks for the accused, and in everyday arguments when you stand up for a person or a view. The pattern is 為…辯護.

column3: It is what someone does when accused or criticized: they offer reasons to clear themselves, as in 无法辩解 and 不必辩解. The neutral word for simply explaining something is 解释.
column4: 他不愿意为自己的错误辩解。
column5: 他不願意為自己的錯誤辯解。
column6: Tā bù yuànyì wèi zìjǐ de cuòwù biànjiě.
column7: He is unwilling to make excuses for his own mistake.
column9: It is what someone does when accused or criticized: they offer reasons to clear themselves, as in 無法辯解 and 不必辯解. The neutral word for simply explaining something is 解釋.

column3: Mostly a philosophical term: 辩证法 is dialectics, and 辩证地看问题 means looking at an issue from both sides instead of only one. It sounds formal and a little academic.
column4: 我们要辩证地看待这个问题。
column5: 我們要辯證地看待這個問題。
column6: Wǒmen yào biànzhèng de kàndài zhège wèntí.
column7: We need to look at this problem dialectically.
column9: Mostly a philosophical term: 辯證法 is dialectics, and 辯證地看問題 means looking at an issue from both sides instead of only one. It sounds formal and a little academic.

column3: It also has a figurative use in the spoken phrases 抓辫子 and 小辫子: someone who has your pigtail in hand can hold a weakness of yours against you.
column4: 她的辫子又黑又长。
column5: 她的辮子又黑又長。
column6: Tā de biànzi yòu hēi yòu cháng.
column7: Her braid is black and long.
column9: It also has a figurative use in the spoken phrases 抓辮子 and 小辮子: someone who has your pigtail in hand can hold a weakness of yours against you.

column3: Lab samples such as blood are also 标本 in hospitals (血液标本); for a statistical or product sample, 样本 is the usual word. 标 once meant the topmost branches of a tree, and 本 is a tree with its roots marked; think of 标本兼治: the symptoms on top, the root cause below.
column4: 博物馆里有很多动物标本。
column5: 博物館裡有很多動物標本。
column6: Bówùguǎn lǐ yǒu hěn duō dòngwù biāoběn.
column7: The museum has many animal specimens.
column9: Lab samples such as blood are also 標本 in hospitals (血液標本); for a statistical or product sample, 樣本 is the usual word. 標 once meant the topmost branches of a tree, and 本 is a tree with its roots marked; think of 標本兼治: the symptoms on top, the root cause below.

column3: It is a mark you put on something so it can be found or told apart later, as in 做标记. In computing it is markup, as in 标记语言.
column4: 我在书上做了一个标记。
column5: 我在書上做了一個標記。
column6: Wǒ zài shū shang zuò le yī gè biāojì.
column7: I made a mark in the book.
column9: It is a mark you put on something so it can be found or told apart later, as in 做標記. In computing it is markup, as in 標記語言.

column3: A formal word for settling a motion by a vote in a meeting, council or legislature: 举手表决, 表决通过. For casting a ballot in an election, 投票 is the word.
column4: 大家举手表决，结果通过了。
column5: 大家舉手表決，結果通過了。
column6: Dàjiā jǔ shǒu biǎojué, jiéguǒ tōngguò le.
column7: Everyone voted by a show of hands, and it passed.
column9: A formal word for settling a motion by a vote in a meeting, council or legislature: 舉手表決, 表決通過. For casting a ballot in an election, 投票 is the word.

column3: Said when someone, often a leader under pressure, must openly take a side on a matter: 公开表态, 迟迟不表态. It splits in two, as in 表个态.
column4: 对这件事，领导还没有表态。
column5: 對這件事，領導還沒有表態。
column6: Duì zhè jiàn shì, lǐngdǎo hái méiyǒu biǎotài.
column7: The leadership has not yet taken a position on this matter.
column9: Said when someone, often a leader under pressure, must openly take a side on a matter: 公開表態, 遲遲不表態. It splits in two, as in 表個態.

column3: Public praise from an organization or authority for someone's good work, often at a ceremony: 表彰大会, 受到表彰, 表彰先进. The one doing it is a group or a leader, not a friend.
column4: 公司表彰了十位优秀员工。
column5: 公司表彰了十位優秀員工。
column6: Gōngsī biǎozhāng le shí wèi yōuxiù yuángōng.
column7: The company commended ten outstanding employees.
column9: Public praise from an organization or authority for someone's good work, often at a ceremony: 表彰大會, 受到表彰, 表彰先進. The one doing it is a group or a leader, not a friend.

column3: A spoken word for holding back something that wants out, such as 憋气 and 憋尿. It also describes bottled-up feelings: 憋了一肚子气, and 憋屈 for feeling stifled and wronged.
column4: 他憋了一肚子气，没有说出来。
column5: 他憋了一肚子氣，沒有說出來。
column6: Tā biē le yī dùzi qì, méiyǒu shuō chūlái.
column7: He was seething inside but did not say it.
column9: A spoken word for holding back something that wants out, such as 憋氣 and 憋尿. It also describes bottled-up feelings: 憋了一肚子氣, and 憋屈 for feeling stifled and wronged.

column3: Originally a second home away from the main residence, hence 度假别墅. Today it also means a big detached house with a garden in an upscale development.
column4: 他们在海边买了一栋别墅。
column5: 他們在海邊買了一棟別墅。
column6: Tāmen zài hǎibiān mǎi le yī dòng biéshù.
column7: They bought a villa by the sea.
column9: Originally a second home away from the main residence, hence 度假別墅. Today it also means a big detached house with a garden in an upscale development.

column3: Always a compliment, for the style of something: 款式别致, 设计别致, a 别致的小店. It praises a design or a decoration, not odd behavior; for a strange person you would say 奇怪.
column4: 这家咖啡店的装饰很别致。
column5: 這家咖啡店的裝飾很別緻。
column6: Zhè jiā kāfēidiàn de zhuāngshì hěn biézhì.
column7: The decor of this cafe is very distinctive.
column9: Always a compliment, for the style of something: 款式別緻, 設計別緻, a 別緻的小店. It praises a design or a decoration, not odd behavior; for a strange person you would say 奇怪.

column3: It describes things that feel wrong, like shoes or a clumsy sentence, and also people being difficult. 闹别扭 is a spat or a sulk between friends, family or a couple.
column4: 这双鞋穿着有点别扭。
column5: 這雙鞋穿著有點彆扭。
column6: Zhè shuāng xié chuānzhe yǒudiǎn bièniu.
column7: These shoes feel a bit awkward to wear.
column9: It describes things that feel wrong, like shoes or a clumsy sentence, and also people being difficult. 鬧彆扭 is a spat or a sulk between friends, family or a couple.

column3: Written and formal, nearly always for something bad about to happen: 濒临灭绝, 濒临破产, 濒临崩溃. It also says a place lies along a sea: 濒临东海. 濒 is pictured as a person standing with their feet at the edge of the water.
column4: 这种动物已经濒临灭绝。
column5: 這種動物已經瀕臨滅絕。
column6: Zhè zhǒng dòngwù yǐjīng bīnlín mièjué.
column7: This animal is already on the verge of extinction.
column9: Written and formal, nearly always for something bad about to happen: 瀕臨滅絕, 瀕臨破產, 瀕臨崩潰. It also says a place lies along a sea: 瀕臨東海. 瀕 is pictured as a person standing with their feet at the edge of the water.

column3: Use 下 for the weather: 下冰雹 means it hails, and 一场冰雹 is a hailstorm. In everyday speech the stones are also called 雹子.
column4: 昨天下了一场冰雹，把玉米都打坏了。
column5: 昨天下了一場冰雹，把玉米都打壞了。
column6: Zuótiān xià le yī chǎng bīngbáo, bǎ yùmǐ dōu dǎ huài le.
column7: A hailstorm yesterday beat all the corn down.
column9: Use 下 for the weather: 下冰雹 means it hails, and 一場冰雹 is a hailstorm. In everyday speech the stones are also called 雹子.

column3: A formal, emphatic way to say "is not" that corrects what someone might assume: 并非如此, 并非所有人. You mostly see it in writing and speeches, rarely in casual talk.
column4: 并非所有人都喜欢这个主意。
column5: 並非所有人都喜歡這個主意。
column6: Bìngfēi suǒyǒu rén dōu xǐhuan zhège zhǔyi.
column7: Not everyone likes this idea.
column9: A formal, emphatic way to say "is not" that corrects what someone might assume: 並非如此, 並非所有人. You mostly see it in writing and speeches, rarely in casual talk.

column3: Used for things of equal rank or standing in parallel: 并列第一 is a tie for first, and 并列句 is a compound sentence. 并 was originally two people standing side by side.
column4: 两个队并列第一。
column5: 兩個隊並列第一。
column6: Liǎng gè duì bìngliè dì yī.
column7: The two teams are tied for first place.
column9: Used for things of equal rank or standing in parallel: 並列第一 is a tie for first, and 並列句 is a compound sentence. 並 was originally two people standing side by side.

column3: A literary word for big surging waves of the sea or a river, as in 波涛汹涌. In plain speech waves are 浪 or 海浪. Taiwan reads 涛 táo.
column4: 船在汹涌的波涛中前进。
column5: 船在洶湧的波濤中前進。
column6: Chuán zài xiōngyǒng de bōtāo zhōng qiánjìn.
column7: The ship moves forward through the surging waves.
column9: A literary word for big surging waves of the sea or a river, as in 波濤洶湧. In plain speech waves are 浪 or 海浪. Taiwan reads 濤 táo.

column3: Mostly used for exploiting workers by living off their labor: 剥削阶级, 剥削工人, 被剥削. It is a political and economic term; for everyday taking advantage of someone, 占便宜 is more usual. When 剥 means peeling, as in 剥皮, it is read bāo. Taiwan reads 削 xuè here.
column4: 他们剥削工人，赚了很多钱。
column5: 他們剝削工人，賺了很多錢。
column6: Tāmen bōxuē gōngrén, zhuàn le hěn duō qián.
column7: They exploited their workers and made a lot of money.
column9: Mostly used for exploiting workers by living off their labor: 剝削階級, 剝削工人, 被剝削. It is a political and economic term; for everyday taking advantage of someone, 佔便宜 is more usual. When 剝 means peeling, as in 剝皮, it is read bāo. Taiwan reads 削 xuè here.

column3: A farming word with a figurative use: 播种希望 is sowing hope, and 播种友谊 spreads friendship, with the idea that it will grow later. 播 goes back to an ancient root meaning to throw away, to cast and to sow. Taiwan reads 播 bò.
column4: 农民在春天忙着播种。
column5: 農民在春天忙著播種。
column6: Nóngmín zài chūntiān mángzhe bōzhǒng.
column7: Farmers are busy sowing in spring.
column9: A farming word with a figurative use: 播種希望 is sowing hope, and 播種友誼 spreads friendship, with the idea that it will grow later. 播 goes back to an ancient root meaning to throw away, to cast and to sow. Taiwan reads 播 bò.

column3: A written phrase of high praise, mostly said of a culture or body of learning, as in 博大精深的中华文化; for a learned person 学识渊博 is more usual.
column4: 中国的传统文化博大精深。
column5: 中國的傳統文化博大精深。
column6: Zhōngguó de chuántǒng wénhuà bódàjīngshēn.
column7: Traditional Chinese culture is vast and profound.
column9: A written phrase of high praise, mostly said of a culture or body of learning, as in 博大精深的中華文化; for a learned person 學識淵博 is more usual.

column3: A hard, close fight, with bare hands or weapons, against a person or a beast: 与歹徒搏斗. It also fits a struggle against something hard, such as 与病魔搏斗. It is heavier than 打架, a brawl.
column4: 他和歹徒搏斗了很久。
column5: 他和歹徒搏鬥了很久。
column6: Tā hé dǎitú bódòu le hěn jiǔ.
column7: He fought with the criminal for a long time.
column9: A hard, close fight, with bare hands or weapons, against a person or a beast: 與歹徒搏鬥. It also fits a struggle against something hard, such as 與病魔搏鬥. It is heavier than 打架, a brawl.

column3: It means fixing a mistake or damage after it has happened, with 措施, 办法 or 工作: 采取补救措施. The thing fixed can follow directly: 补救错误, 补救损失.
column4: 他想尽办法补救自己的错误。
column5: 他想盡辦法補救自己的錯誤。
column6: Tā xiǎng jìn bànfǎ bǔjiù zìjǐ de cuòwù.
column7: He tried every way to make up for his mistake.
column9: It means fixing a mistake or damage after it has happened, with 措施, 辦法 or 工作: 採取補救措施. The thing fixed can follow directly: 補救錯誤, 補救損失.

column3: It suits catching something quick or elusive: insects and small animals (捕捉蝴蝶), and also abstract things like 捕捉灵感, 捕捉机会 and 捕捉表情.
column4: 摄影师捕捉到了精彩的一瞬间。
column5: 攝影師捕捉到了精彩的一瞬間。
column6: Shèyǐngshī bǔzhuō dào le jīngcǎi de yī shùnjiān.
column7: The photographer caught a wonderful moment.
column9: It suits catching something quick or elusive: insects and small animals (捕捉蝴蝶), and also abstract things like 捕捉靈感, 捕捉機會 and 捕捉表情.

column3: Mostly met in 哺乳动物, the mammals, and in 哺乳期, the period of nursing a baby. In plain speech, nursing a baby is 喂奶.
column4: 鲸是哺乳动物，不是鱼。
column5: 鯨是哺乳動物，不是魚。
column6: Jīng shì bǔrǔ dòngwù, bù shì yú.
column7: Whales are mammals, not fish.
column9: Mostly met in 哺乳動物, the mammals, and in 哺乳期, the period of nursing a baby. In plain speech, nursing a baby is 餵奶.

column3: A written word used in set phrases. After a negative adjective it adds "utterly": 疲惫不堪, 狼狈不堪. Before a verb or noun it means unable to bear it: 不堪一击, 不堪重负.
column4: 他连续加班，已经疲惫不堪。
column5: 他連續加班，已經疲憊不堪。
column6: Tā liánxù jiābān, yǐjīng píbèi bùkān.
column7: He has worked overtime for days and is utterly worn out.
column9: A written word used in set phrases. After a negative adjective it adds "utterly": 疲憊不堪, 狼狽不堪. Before a verb or noun it means unable to bear it: 不堪一擊, 不堪重負.

column3: Used for anything that astonishes, good or bad: a miracle, a coincidence, a strange habit. It works as a predicate (真不可思议) or before 的 to modify a noun (不可思议的事). On its own, 思议 is usually used in the negative.
column4: 他一个人就完成了全部工作，真不可思议。
column5: 他一個人就完成了全部工作，真不可思議。
column6: Tā yī gè rén jiù wánchéng le quánbù gōngzuò, zhēn bùkěsīyì.
column7: He finished all the work by himself, which is incredible.
column9: Used for anything that astonishes, good or bad: a miracle, a coincidence, a strange habit. It works as a predicate (真不可思議) or before 的 to modify a noun (不可思議的事). On its own, 思議 is usually used in the negative.

column3: A compliment that nearly always comes right before 是 and a title or reputation: 不愧是冠军, 不愧是老师. It says that someone's performance lives up to what they are known as. It is praise, though 真不愧是你 can also be said with a wink about someone's bad habit. In writing it is also 不愧为.
column4: 你不愧是中文老师，发音真标准。
column5: 你不愧是中文老師，發音真標準。
column6: Nǐ bùkuì shì Zhōngwén lǎoshī, fāyīn zhēn biāozhǔn.
column7: You really are a Chinese teacher, your pronunciation is so standard.
column9: A compliment that nearly always comes right before 是 and a title or reputation: 不愧是冠軍, 不愧是老師. It says that someone's performance lives up to what they are known as. It is praise, though 真不愧是你 can also be said with a wink about someone's bad habit. In writing it is also 不愧為.

column3: A fairly formal verb that sets up a big sacrifice made for a goal. It is followed by a cost or by an action: 不惜代价, 不惜一切, 不惜牺牲. The goal usually comes first or after 为了. Taiwan reads 惜 as xí, so the word is bù xí there.
column4: 他不惜一切代价救出了孩子。
column5: 他不惜一切代價救出了孩子。
column6: Tā bùxī yīqiè dàijià jiùchū le háizi.
column7: He saved the child at any cost.
column9: A fairly formal verb that sets up a big sacrifice made for a goal. It is followed by a cost or by an action: 不惜代價, 不惜一切, 不惜犧牲. The goal usually comes first or after 為了. Taiwan reads 惜 as xí, so the word is bù xí there.

column3: It describes two or more people or things at about the same level, and it is the predicate of the sentence: 水平不相上下, 年龄不相上下. The subject must be plural or a pair (他们俩, 两队), because the idiom compares them with each other. It is used in speech and in writing.
column4: 他们两个人的成绩不相上下。
column5: 他們兩個人的成績不相上下。
column6: Tāmen liǎng gè rén de chéngjì bùxiāngshàngxià.
column7: The two of them have about the same grades.
column9: It describes two or more people or things at about the same level, and it is the predicate of the sentence: 水平不相上下, 年齡不相上下. The subject must be plural or a pair (他們倆, 兩隊), because the idiom compares them with each other. It is used in speech and in writing.

column3: A scolding. It reacts to behavior that crosses a line (迟到两个小时, 乱扔垃圾) or to something excessive, such as a price. It can be said to someone directly (你太不像话了) or about a situation. The positive 像话 is mostly heard in questions like 这像话吗?
column4: 他迟到了两个小时，真不像话！
column5: 他遲到了兩個小時，真不像話！
column6: Tā chídào le liǎng gè xiǎoshí, zhēn bùxiànghuà!
column7: He was two hours late, it is outrageous!
column9: A scolding. It reacts to behavior that crosses a line (遲到兩個小時, 亂扔垃圾) or to something excessive, such as a price. It can be said to someone directly (你太不像話了) or about a situation. The positive 像話 is mostly heard in questions like 這像話嗎?

column3: Describes open disdain: not even glancing at something you think beneath you, such as advice, criticism, an offer, or fame and money. The thing comes after 对. Whether that is arrogance or admirable depends on the thing.
column4: 他对批评不屑一顾，继续做自己的事。
column5: 他對批評不屑一顧，繼續做自己的事。
column6: Tā duì pīpíng bùxièyīgù, jìxù zuò zìjǐ de shì.
column7: He brushed off the criticism and kept doing his own thing.
column9: Describes open disdain: not even glancing at something you think beneath you, such as advice, criticism, an offer, or fame and money. The thing comes after 對. Whether that is arrogance or admirable depends on the thing.

column3: It is usually the predicate of a clause, often as 是不言而喻的, or it opens a statement that supports what comes next: 不言而喻，这件事很重要. Rather formal and common in writing and speeches; in casual talk people say 那还用说.
column4: 这个道理是不言而喻的。
column5: 這個道理是不言而喻的。
column6: Zhège dàolǐ shì bùyán'éryù de.
column7: This principle goes without saying.
column9: It is usually the predicate of a clause, often as 是不言而喻的, or it opens a statement that supports what comes next: 不言而喻，這件事很重要. Rather formal and common in writing and speeches; in casual talk people say 那還用説.

column3: Always critical. It describes someone who will use any method, however dishonest or cruel, to get what they want. It often takes 地 before a verb (不择手段地竞争) and goes with 为了. 手段 alone can be a neutral "method", but it also carries a hint of tricks.
column4: 他为了成功不择手段。
column5: 他為了成功不擇手段。
column6: Tā wèile chénggōng bùzéshǒuduàn.
column7: He will stop at nothing to succeed.
column9: Always critical. It describes someone who will use any method, however dishonest or cruel, to get what they want. It often takes 地 before a verb (不擇手段地競爭) and goes with 為了. 手段 alone can be a neutral "method", but it also carries a hint of tricks.

column3: Both a noun and a verb. It covers the layout of a room, a garden or a page, and also the way a company or a government sets out its plans: 整体布局, 战略布局, 全球布局. In board games, a 布局 is the opening setup.
column4: 这个房间的布局很合理。
column5: 這個房間的佈局很合理。
column6: Zhège fángjiān de bùjú hěn hélǐ.
column7: The layout of this room is very sensible.
column9: Both a noun and a verb. It covers the layout of a room, a garden or a page, and also the way a company or a government sets out its plans: 整體佈局, 戰略佈局, 全球佈局. In board games, a 佈局 is the opening setup.

column3: Literally the pace of someone walking or marching (步伐整齐, 步伐轻快), but now mostly figurative, for the pace of progress or change: 加快步伐, 跟上时代的步伐, 步伐一致. Taiwan reads 伐 as fā.
column4: 公司正在加快发展的步伐。
column5: 公司正在加快發展的步伐。
column6: Gōngsī zhèngzài jiākuài fāzhǎn de bùfá.
column7: The company is picking up the pace of its growth.
column9: Literally the pace of someone walking or marching (步伐整齊, 步伐輕快), but now mostly figurative, for the pace of progress or change: 加快步伐, 跟上時代的步伐, 步伐一致. Taiwan reads 伐 as fā.

column3: A verb and a noun for planning out and assigning people, troops or tasks: 部署工作, 战略部署. In computing it is the usual word for deploying software, as in 部署服务器. Taiwan reads 署 as shù.
column4: 公司已经部署了新的系统。
column5: 公司已經部署了新的系統。
column6: Gōngsī yǐjīng bùshǔ le xīn de xìtǒng.
column7: The company has already rolled out the new system.
column9: A verb and a noun for planning out and assigning people, troops or tasks: 部署工作, 戰略部署. In computing it is the usual word for deploying software, as in 部署服務器. Taiwan reads 署 as shù.

column3: It praises practical ability, the kind a person shows in handling work and people: 有才干, 增长才干, 才干出众. It is said of a manager, an official or a young person with promise, and is a little more formal than 能力.
column4: 他年轻，但很有才干。
column5: 他年輕，但很有才幹。
column6: Tā niánqīng, dàn hěn yǒu cáigàn.
column7: He is young, but very capable.
column9: It praises practical ability, the kind a person shows in handling work and people: 有才幹, 增長才幹, 才幹出眾. It is said of a manager, an official or a young person with promise, and is a little more formal than 能力.

column3: The money matters of a company or organization: accounts, budgets, reports. It is common in compounds such as 财务部, 财务报表, 财务经理. Public money of a government is 财政, and managing your own money is 理财.
column4: 财务部负责公司的账目。
column5: 財務部負責公司的帳目。
column6: Cáiwù bù fùzé gōngsī de zhàngmù.
column7: The finance department is in charge of the company's accounts.
column9: The money matters of a company or organization: accounts, budgets, reports. It is common in compounds such as 財務部, 財務報表, 財務經理. Public money of a government is 財政, and managing your own money is 理財.

column3: Finance on the level of the state or a local government: taxes, the budget and spending. Typical compounds are 财政部, 财政收入, 财政赤字. For a company's money, say 财务.
column4: 今年的财政收入增加了。
column5: 今年的財政收入增加了。
column6: Jīnnián de cáizhèng shōurù zēngjiā le.
column7: This year's government revenue has gone up.
column9: Finance on the level of the state or a local government: taxes, the budget and spending. Typical compounds are 財政部, 財政收入, 財政赤字. For a company's money, say 財務.

column3: A person who makes clothes to order or alters them: 裁缝店 is a tailor shop, and you take pants to a 裁缝 to be shortened. The word is used for a man or a woman. Read cáiféng, with a full second tone, the same word is a verb meaning to tailor clothes.
column4: 我请裁缝把裤子改短了。
column5: 我請裁縫把褲子改短了。
column6: Wǒ qǐng cáifeng bǎ kùzi gǎi duǎn le.
column7: I had the tailor shorten my pants.
column9: A person who makes clothes to order or alters them: 裁縫店 is a tailor shop, and you take pants to a 裁縫 to be shortened. The word is used for a man or a woman. Read cáiféng, with a full second tone, the same word is a verb meaning to tailor clothes.

column3: To collect things in an organized way, by hand or with tools: specimens, samples, plants, or data: 采集标本, 采集数据, 采集样本. It suits fieldwork and research more than shopping or casual picking. 采 shows a hand picking from a tree.
column4: 研究人员正在采集水样。
column5: 研究人員正在採集水樣。
column6: Yánjiū rényuán zhèngzài cǎijí shuǐyàng.
column7: The researchers are collecting water samples.
column9: To collect things in an organized way, by hand or with tools: specimens, samples, plants, or data: 採集標本, 採集數據, 採集樣本. It suits fieldwork and research more than shopping or casual picking. 採 shows a hand picking from a tree.

column3: In the military, a staff officer. In everyday talk it means someone who gives advice, and the verb is used in a relaxed way, often doubled: 帮我参谋参谋 means "help me decide" about a purchase or a plan.
column4: 你帮我参谋参谋，这件衣服好看吗？
column5: 你幫我參謀參謀，這件衣服好看嗎？
column6: Nǐ bāng wǒ cānmóu cānmóu, zhè jiàn yīfu hǎokàn ma?
column7: Help me decide: does this piece of clothing look good?
column9: In the military, a staff officer. In everyday talk it means someone who gives advice, and the verb is used in a relaxed way, often doubled: 幫我參謀參謀 means "help me decide" about a purchase or a plan.

column3: A formal verb for following or checking against a model, rule or earlier document: 参照标准, 参照执行, 请参照说明书. It is common in official notices and instructions.
column4: 请参照说明书安装。
column5: 請參照說明書安裝。
column6: Qǐng cānzhào shuōmíngshū ānzhuāng.
column7: Please install it following the manual.
column9: A formal verb for following or checking against a model, rule or earlier document: 參照標準, 參照執行, 請參照說明書. It is common in official notices and instructions.

column3: What is left behind after something has been processed or has passed, and usually unwanted: 农药残留, 残留物, 残留的污渍. As a verb it also covers lingering traces of a feeling or a habit.
column4: 蔬菜上可能有农药残留。
column5: 蔬菜上可能有農藥殘留。
column6: Shūcài shàng kěnéng yǒu nóngyào cánliú.
column7: There may be pesticide residue on vegetables.
column9: What is left behind after something has been processed or has passed, and usually unwanted: 農藥殘留, 殘留物, 殘留的污漬. As a verb it also covers lingering traces of a feeling or a habit.

column3: It describes people or acts that cause suffering without pity: a cruel method, a merciless ruler, abuse of animals. It is also used for a hard truth or a hard choice: 太残忍了 means "that is too harsh", and 对…残忍 names who is hurt.
column4: 虐待动物是很残忍的。
column5: 虐待動物是很殘忍的。
column6: Nüèdài dòngwù shì hěn cánrěn de.
column7: Abusing animals is very cruel.
column9: It describes people or acts that cause suffering without pity: a cruel method, a merciless ruler, abuse of animals. It is also used for a hard truth or a hard choice: 太殘忍了 means "that is too harsh", and 對…殘忍 names who is hurt.

column3: A bright, upbeat word for sunshine, light, smiles, and by extension a culture or a future: 灿烂的阳光, 灿烂的笑容, 灿烂的文化, 前途灿烂. It is always positive.
column4: 她脸上露出了灿烂的笑容。
column5: 她臉上露出了燦爛的笑容。
column6: Tā liǎn shàng lùchū le cànlàn de xiàoróng.
column7: A bright smile appeared on her face.
column9: A bright, upbeat word for sunshine, light, smiles, and by extension a culture or a future: 燦爛的陽光, 燦爛的笑容, 燦爛的文化, 前途燦爛. It is always positive.

column3: For something done in a hurry, without time to prepare, and so with a hint that the result is not good: 仓促决定, 仓促离开, 仓促应战. It can also be the predicate: 时间太仓促了.
column4: 时间太仓促了，我没来得及准备。
column5: 時間太倉促了，我沒來得及準備。
column6: Shíjiān tài cāngcù le, wǒ méi láidejí zhǔnbèi.
column7: There was too little time, and I could not prepare.
column9: For something done in a hurry, without time to prepare, and so with a hint that the result is not good: 倉促決定, 倉促離開, 倉促應戰. It can also be the predicate: 時間太倉促了.

column3: Most often of a face that has lost its color through illness, fear or tiredness: 脸色苍白. It is also used figuratively for words, arguments and writing that are weak and empty: 苍白无力.
column4: 他的脸色苍白，好像生病了。
column5: 他的臉色蒼白，好像生病了。
column6: Tā de liǎnsè cāngbái, hǎoxiàng shēngbìng le.
column7: His face is pale, as if he were sick.
column9: Most often of a face that has lost its color through illness, fear or tiredness: 臉色蒼白. It is also used figuratively for words, arguments and writing that are weak and empty: 蒼白無力.

column3: A bound character: you rarely see it alone, but in compounds for a space inside a ship or an aircraft: 机舱 (an aircraft cabin), 船舱, 客舱 (the passenger cabin), 货舱 (the hold), 头等舱 (first class).
column4: 乘客们陆续走进了机舱。
column5: 乘客們陸續走進了機艙。
column6: Chéngkèmen lùxù zǒujìn le jī cāng.
column7: The passengers filed into the cabin.
column9: A bound character: you rarely see it alone, but in compounds for a space inside a ship or an aircraft: 機艙 (an aircraft cabin), 船艙, 客艙 (the passenger cabin), 貨艙 (the hold), 頭等艙 (first class).

column3: To work hard and wear yourself out looking after things, often for a family or for others: 为家操劳, 操劳过度. People use it with warmth about parents and elders, and also about officials who work long hours for the public.
column4: 母亲一辈子为这个家操劳。
column5: 母親一輩子為這個家操勞。
column6: Mǔqīn yībèizi wèi zhège jiā cāoláo.
column7: My mother worked hard for this family her whole life.
column9: To work hard and wear yourself out looking after things, often for a family or for others: 為家操勞, 操勞過度. People use it with warmth about parents and elders, and also about officials who work long hours for the public.

column3: Mostly for group drills, such as soldiers or a team practicing a routine, and for going over a skill again and again. For everyday practice, 练习 is the usual word.
column4: 士兵们每天早上都在操场上操练。
column5: 士兵們每天早上都在操場上操練。
column6: Shìbīngmen měitiān zǎoshang dōu zài cāochǎng shàng cāoliàn.
column7: The soldiers drill on the parade ground every morning.
column9: Mostly for group drills, such as soldiers or a team practicing a routine, and for going over a skill again and again. For everyday practice, 練習 is the usual word.

column3: Describes a place or its sound, such as a market, a street or a hall full of voices and clatter (环境嘈杂, 人声嘈杂). To say a person is loud, use 吵.
column4: 市场里人声嘈杂。
column5: 市場裡人聲嘈雜。
column6: Shìchǎng lǐ rénshēng cáozá.
column7: The market is noisy with voices.
column9: Describes a place or its sound, such as a market, a street or a hall full of voices and clatter (環境嘈雜, 人聲嘈雜). To say a person is loud, use 吵.

column3: A draft of a law, rule, plan or agreement that has not yet been approved, as in 法律草案 and 预算草案. A draft of an essay or letter is 草稿.
column4: 委员会正在讨论新法律的草案。
column5: 委員會正在討論新法律的草案。
column6: Wěiyuánhuì zhèngzài tǎolùn xīn fǎlǜ de cǎo'àn.
column7: The committee is discussing the draft of the new law.
column9: A draft of a law, rule, plan or agreement that has not yet been approved, as in 法律草案 and 預算草案. A draft of an essay or letter is 草稿.

column3: A criticism of a decision or a piece of work done in a hurry, without thinking it through: 草率的决定, 草率行事, or simply 太草率了.
column4: 这个决定太草率了。
column5: 這個決定太草率了。
column6: Zhège juédìng tài cǎoshuài le.
column7: This decision was too hasty.
column9: A criticism of a decision or a piece of work done in a hurry, without thinking it through: 草率的決定, 草率行事, or simply 太草率了.

column3: Besides a physical side, it is used for one side of a matter. 从侧面了解 means finding out indirectly, from other people or other evidence, not from the person involved.
column4: 他从侧面了解了这件事。
column5: 他從側面了解了這件事。
column6: Tā cóng cèmiàn liǎojiě le zhè jiàn shì.
column7: He learned about the matter indirectly.
column9: Besides a physical side, it is used for one side of a matter. 從側面了解 means finding out indirectly, from other people or other evidence, not from the person involved.

column3: A written, fairly formal idiom for things that keep appearing one after another, such as new products, new tricks or new problems; the thing comes first: 新问题层出不穷. Literally, layer after layer comes out and never runs dry.
column4: 网络诈骗手段层出不穷。
column5: 網路詐騙手段層出不窮。
column6: Wǎngluò zhàpiàn shǒuduàn céngchūbùqióng.
column7: Online scam methods keep emerging, one after another.
column9: A written, fairly formal idiom for things that keep appearing one after another, such as new products, new tricks or new problems; the thing comes first: 新問題層出不窮. Literally, layer after layer comes out and never runs dry.

column3: The socket in the wall or on a power strip that you plug into. The plug on the end of the cord is 插头. A power strip is 插线板 on the mainland and 延长线 in Taiwan.
column4: 这个插座坏了，手机充不了电。
column5: 這個插座壞了，手機充不了電。
column6: Zhège chāzuò huài le, shǒujī chōng bùliǎo diàn.
column7: This outlet is broken, so I can't charge my phone.
column9: The socket in the wall or on a power strip that you plug into. The plug on the end of the cord is 插頭. A power strip is 插線板 on the mainland and 延長線 in Taiwan.

column3: News and police language: what is found and seized comes after it, as in 查获毒品 and 查获走私货物. It is the authorities who 查获, never an ordinary person finding something.
column4: 海关查获了一批走私香烟。
column5: 海關查獲了一批走私香菸。
column6: Hǎiguān cháhuò le yī pī zǒusī xiāngyān.
column7: Customs seized a batch of smuggled cigarettes.
column9: News and police language: what is found and seized comes after it, as in 查獲毒品 and 查獲走私貨物. It is the authorities who 查獲, never an ordinary person finding something.

column3: Rarely stands alone. It lives in words such as 岔路 (a fork in the road), 打岔 (to cut in on someone talking) and 岔开话题 (to change the subject).
column4: 别打岔，让他把话说完。
column5: 別打岔，讓他把話說完。
column6: Bié dǎ chà, ràng tā bǎ huà shuōwán.
column7: Don't interrupt; let him finish speaking.
column9: Rarely stands alone. It lives in words such as 岔路 (a fork in the road), 打岔 (to cut in on someone talking) and 岔開話題 (to change the subject).

column3: Most often as 一刹那 or 刹那间, a slightly literary way to say in an instant. The word is a sound-for-sound borrowing of the Sanskrit word for an instant.
column4: 一刹那，所有的灯都灭了。
column5: 一剎那，所有的燈都滅了。
column6: Yī chànà, suǒyǒu de dēng dōu miè le.
column7: In an instant, all the lights went out.
column9: Most often as 一剎那 or 剎那間, a slightly literary way to say in an instant. The word is a sound-for-sound borrowing of the Sanskrit word for an instant.

column3: Surprise mixed with puzzlement at something unexpected. Typical frames are 感到诧异 and 令人诧异, and it reads more written than 吃惊.
column4: 他的回答让我感到很诧异。
column5: 他的回答讓我感到很詫異。
column6: Tā de huídá ràng wǒ gǎndào hěn chàyì.
column7: His answer surprised me a great deal.
column9: Surprise mixed with puzzlement at something unexpected. Typical frames are 感到詫異 and 令人詫異, and it reads more written than 吃驚.

column3: 油 is any fuel oil: 汽油 is gasoline, 柴油 diesel, and 加油 to fill up the tank.
column4: 这辆卡车用的是柴油。
column5: 這輛卡車用的是柴油。
column6: Zhè liàng kǎchē yòng de shì cháiyóu.
column7: This truck runs on diesel.
column9: 油 is any fuel oil: 汽油 is gasoline, 柴油 diesel, and 加油 to fill up the tank.

column3: You 搀 someone who is weak, old, hurt or tipsy by holding an arm, most often in 搀扶: 搀着老人过马路 is helping an old person across the street.
column4: 他搀着奶奶慢慢地走。
column5: 他攙著奶奶慢慢地走。
column6: Tā chān zhe nǎinai mànmàn de zǒu.
column7: He held grandma's arm and walked slowly.
column9: You 攙 someone who is weak, old, hurt or tipsy by holding an arm, most often in 攙扶: 攙著老人過馬路 is helping an old person across the street.

column3: Describes someone who craves a particular food or loves to eat: 嘴馋, 馋猫 (a greedy cat, said of a person who loves food) and 馋得流口水. It can also be a verb: 我馋火锅了.
column4: 看到蛋糕，孩子馋得直流口水。
column5: 看到蛋糕，孩子饞得直流口水。
column6: Kàndào dàngāo, háizi chán de zhí liú kǒushuǐ.
column7: Seeing the cake, the child drooled with longing.
column9: Describes someone who craves a particular food or loves to eat: 嘴饞, 饞貓 (a greedy cat, said of a person who loves food) and 饞得流口水. It can also be a verb: 我饞火鍋了.

column3: Said of vines, cords or thread winding around something, and also of worries, illness or a problem that will not let go of a person: 被问题缠绕.
column4: 藤蔓缠绕在老树上。
column5: 藤蔓纏繞在老樹上。
column6: Téngmàn chánrào zài lǎoshù shàng.
column7: The vines twine around the old tree.
column9: Said of vines, cords or thread winding around something, and also of worries, illness or a problem that will not let go of a person: 被問題纏繞.

column3: Formal: to lay out a view, theory, plan or position at some length, in speech or writing (阐述观点, 阐述立场). In casual talk, 解释 or 说明 is more natural.
column4: 他在会上详细阐述了公司的计划。
column5: 他在會上詳細闡述了公司的計畫。
column6: Tā zài huì shàng xiángxì chǎnshù le gōngsī de jìhuà.
column7: At the meeting he explained the company's plan in detail.
column9: Formal: to lay out a view, theory, plan or position at some length, in speech or writing (闡述觀點, 闡述立場). In casual talk, 解釋 or 說明 is more natural.

column3: The body or the voice shaking from cold, fear, anger or strong feeling: 浑身颤抖, 声音颤抖. It describes a continuing tremble, not a single jolt. Taiwan reads the first character zhàn.
column4: 他冷得浑身颤抖。
column5: 他冷得渾身顫抖。
column6: Tā lěng de húnshēn chàndǒu.
column7: He was shivering all over from the cold.
column9: The body or the voice shaking from cold, fear, anger or strong feeling: 渾身顫抖, 聲音顫抖. It describes a continuing tremble, not a single jolt. Taiwan reads the first character zhàn.

column3: Formal and written, for paying back debts, loans or what one owes: 偿还债务, 偿还贷款. In daily speech you simply say 还钱. Here 还 is read huán, pay back; read hái, it means still.
column4: 他每个月都按时偿还贷款。
column5: 他每個月都按時償還貸款。
column6: Tā měi gè yuè dōu ànshí chánghuán dàikuǎn.
column7: He pays back his loan on time every month.
column9: Formal and written, for paying back debts, loans or what one owes: 償還債務, 償還貸款. In daily speech you simply say 還錢. Here 還 is read huán, pay back; read hái, it means still.

column3: Opened wide and left that way: a door, a window or a coat. It is also used for the heart: 敞开心扉 means to open up and speak frankly, and 敞开胸怀 means to be open-minded.
column4: 门敞开着，屋里一个人也没有。
column5: 門敞開著，屋裡一個人也沒有。
column6: Mén chǎngkāi zhe, wūlǐ yī gè rén yě méiyǒu.
column7: The door was wide open and there was nobody inside.
column9: Opened wide and left that way: a door, a window or a coat. It is also used for the heart: 敞開心扉 means to open up and speak frankly, and 敞開胸懷 means to be open-minded.

column3: Said of books, records and products that are selling well: 畅销书 is a bestseller, and 畅销全球 means selling around the world. The opposite is 滞销.
column4: 这本书在国外也很畅销。
column5: 這本書在國外也很暢銷。
column6: Zhè běn shū zài guówài yě hěn chàngxiāo.
column7: This book also sells well abroad.
column9: Said of books, records and products that are selling well: 暢銷書 is a bestseller, and 暢銷全球 means selling around the world. The opposite is 滯銷.

column3: A verb and a noun, used by governments, organizations or groups: 发出倡议 is to issue a call, and a 倡议书 is a written call to action. Formal; between friends you would say 提议.
column4: 学校倡议大家节约用水。
column5: 學校倡議大家節約用水。
column6: Xuéxiào chàngyì dàjiā jiéyuē yòng shuǐ.
column7: The school urges everyone to save water.
column9: A verb and a noun, used by governments, organizations or groups: 發出倡議 is to issue a call, and a 倡議書 is a written call to action. Formal; between friends you would say 提議.

column3: Mostly figurative, for the hideout of criminals, bandits or enemies (匪徒的巢穴, 敌人的巢穴). For an animal's home, 窝 or 巢 is the everyday word.
column4: 警察端掉了毒贩的巢穴。
column5: 警察端掉了毒販的巢穴。
column6: Jǐngchá duāndiào le dúfàn de cháoxué.
column7: The police wiped out the drug dealers' hideout.
column9: Mostly figurative, for the hideout of criminals, bandits or enemies (匪徒的巢穴, 敵人的巢穴). For an animal's home, 窩 or 巢 is the everyday word.

column3: The period of one ruling family: 哪个朝代 asks which dynasty, and 朝代更替 is a change of dynasty. A single dynasty is its name plus 朝, as in 唐朝 and 明朝.
column4: 唐朝是中国历史上最强盛的朝代之一。
column5: 唐朝是中國歷史上最強盛的朝代之一。
column6: Tángcháo shì Zhōngguó lìshǐ shàng zuì qiángshèng de cháodài zhī yī.
column7: The Tang is one of the most powerful dynasties in Chinese history.
column9: The period of one ruling family: 哪個朝代 asks which dynasty, and 朝代更替 is a change of dynasty. A single dynasty is its name plus 朝, as in 唐朝 and 明朝.

column3: You 嘲笑 a person or their flaw or mistake, with contempt: 嘲笑别人, 被嘲笑. It is harsher than 取笑, which is closer to teasing.
column4: 不要嘲笑别人的错误。
column5: 不要嘲笑別人的錯誤。
column6: Bùyào cháoxiào biérén de cuòwù.
column7: Don't laugh at other people's mistakes.
column9: You 嘲笑 a person or their flaw or mistake, with contempt: 嘲笑別人, 被嘲笑. It is harsher than 取笑, which is closer to teasing.

column3: Mostly military or organized: troops, police or staff pulling out of a position, often on orders. Stepping back with your feet is 后退.
column4: 部队接到命令，连夜撤退。
column5: 部隊接到命令，連夜撤退。
column6: Bùduì jiēdào mìnglìng, liányè chètuì.
column7: The troops received the order and retreated overnight.
column9: Mostly military or organized: troops, police or staff pulling out of a position, often on orders. Stepping back with your feet is 後退.

column3: Used for sediment in chemistry, and very often figuratively: experience, feelings or ideas 沉淀 as time passes, typically in the pattern 沉淀下来.
column4: 经过多年的沉淀，他变得成熟了。
column5: 經過多年的沉澱，他變得成熟了。
column6: Jīngguò duōnián de chéndiàn, tā biànde chéngshú le.
column7: After years of reflection, he has grown more mature.
column9: Used for sediment in chemistry, and very often figuratively: experience, feelings or ideas 沉澱 as time passes, typically in the pattern 沉澱下來.

column3: Describes what feels heavy and airless: the mood of a meeting, a dull routine, gloomy weather or a muffled sound; typical partners are 气氛, 天气 and 声音. On its own, 闷 is also read mēn, for something stuffy or shut indoors.
column4: 会议的气氛很沉闷。
column5: 會議的氣氛很沉悶。
column6: Huìyì de qìfēn hěn chénmèn.
column7: The atmosphere at the meeting was dreary.
column9: Describes what feels heavy and airless: the mood of a meeting, a dull routine, gloomy weather or a muffled sound; typical partners are 氣氛, 天氣 and 聲音. On its own, 悶 is also read mēn, for something stuffy or shut indoors.

column3: A somewhat literary word, most often in 陷入沉思 (fall into deep thought) or 沉思片刻 (ponder for a moment).
column4: 他坐在窗前，陷入了沉思。
column5: 他坐在窗前，陷入了沉思。
column6: Tā zuò zài chuāngqián, xiànrù le chénsī.
column7: He sat by the window, lost in thought.
column9: A somewhat literary word, most often in 陷入沉思 (fall into deep thought) or 沉思片刻 (ponder for a moment).

column3: Praise for someone who keeps a clear head under pressure, often in 沉着冷静 or 沉着应对 (respond calmly).
column4: 面对危险，他依然沉着冷静。
column5: 面對危險，他依然沉著冷靜。
column6: Miànduì wēixiǎn, tā yīrán chénzhuó lěngjìng.
column7: Facing danger, he still stayed calm and collected.
column9: Praise for someone who keeps a clear head under pressure, often in 沉著冷靜 or 沉著應對 (respond calmly).

column3: Usually a criticism. It goes with things that should have been replaced: 设备 (equipment), 观念 (ideas), 方法 (methods) and 思想 (thinking).
column4: 这些设备已经很陈旧了。
column5: 這些設備已經很陳舊了。
column6: Zhèxiē shèbèi yǐjīng hěn chénjiù le.
column7: This equipment is already very outdated.
column9: Usually a criticism. It goes with things that should have been replaced: 設備 (equipment), 觀念 (ideas), 方法 (methods) and 思想 (thinking).

column3: A formal word for laying out facts or views in court, at a meeting or in writing: 陈述事实, 陈述理由, 陈述意见. In grammar, 陈述句 is a declarative sentence.
column4: 他向法官陈述了事情的经过。
column5: 他向法官陳述了事情的經過。
column6: Tā xiàng fǎguān chénshù le shìqing de jīngguò.
column7: He told the judge how the events unfolded.
column9: A formal word for laying out facts or views in court, at a meeting or in writing: 陳述事實, 陳述理由, 陳述意見. In grammar, 陳述句 is a declarative sentence.

column3: A background makes something else stand out: A 衬托 B, or the frequent pattern 在……的衬托下 (set off by …). Red flowers are set off by green leaves (红花还要绿叶衬托).
column4: 在蓝天的衬托下，白云显得更白了。
column5: 在藍天的襯托下，白雲顯得更白了。
column6: Zài lántiān de chèntuō xià, báiyún xiǎnde gèng bái le.
column7: Set off by the blue sky, the white clouds look even whiter.
column9: A background makes something else stand out: A 襯托 B, or the frequent pattern 在……的襯托下 (set off by …). Red flowers are set off by green leaves (紅花還要綠葉襯托).

column3: An idiom for getting just what you hoped for: a job, a home, a purchase. It is also a common good wish: 祝你称心如意. 称 is read chèn in this word, not chēng as in its meaning "to weigh". Taiwan reads 称 here as chèng.
column4: 她终于找到了称心如意的工作。
column5: 她終於找到了稱心如意的工作。
column6: Tā zhōngyú zhǎodào le chènxīnrúyì de gōngzuò.
