column7: She finally found a job that suits her perfectly.
column9: An idiom for getting just what you hoped for: a job, a home, a purchase. It is also a common good wish: 祝你稱心如意. 稱 is read chèn in this word, not chēng as in its meaning "to weigh". Taiwan reads 稱 here as chèng.

column3: A spoken adverb that goes before a verb, usually with a hint of spite: 成心气我 (do it to annoy me), 成心找麻烦 (look for trouble).
column4: 你是不是成心气我？
column5: 你是不是成心氣我？
column6: Nǐ shì bù shì chéngxīn qì wǒ?
column7: Are you doing this on purpose to annoy me?
column9: A spoken adverb that goes before a verb, usually with a hint of spite: 成心氣我 (do it to annoy me), 成心找麻煩 (look for trouble).

column3: Formal and warm, used before a noun for feelings you put into words: 诚挚的感谢 (thanks), 诚挚的问候 (greetings), 诚挚的友谊 (friendship).
column4: 我要向你表示诚挚的感谢。
column5: 我要向你表示誠摯的感謝。
column6: Wǒ yào xiàng nǐ biǎoshì chéngzhì de gǎnxiè.
column7: I want to express my sincere thanks to you.
column9: Formal and warm, used before a noun for feelings you put into words: 誠摯的感謝 (thanks), 誠摯的問候 (greetings), 誠摯的友誼 (friendship).

column3: Used for taking on a construction job, a piece of land or a shop under a contract: 承包工程, 承包土地. The party that does it is the 承包商. 承 shows a kneeling person with both hands, holding something up.
column4: 这家公司承包了新大楼的建设。
column5: 這家公司承包了新大樓的建設。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī chéngbāo le xīn dàlóu de jiànshè.
column7: This company took the contract to build the new building.
column9: Used for taking on a construction job, a piece of land or a shop under a contract: 承包工程, 承包土地. The party that does it is the 承包商. 承 shows a kneeling person with both hands, holding something up.

column3: The castle of fairy tales and European history, as in 童话里的城堡. A Chinese city wall is a 城墙, and an old walled town a 古城.
column4: 山顶上有一座古老的城堡。
column5: 山頂上有一座古老的城堡。
column6: Shāndǐng shàng yǒu yī zuò gǔlǎo de chéngbǎo.
column7: There is an old castle on top of the mountain.
column9: The castle of fairy tales and European history, as in 童話裡的城堡. A Chinese city wall is a 城牆, and an old walled town a 古城.

column3: A verb for putting food into a bowl or plate: 盛饭, 盛汤, 盛一碗. The other reading, shèng, means flourishing.
column4: 请帮我盛一碗汤。
column5: 請幫我盛一碗湯。
column6: Qǐng bāng wǒ chéng yī wǎn tāng.
column7: Please ladle me a bowl of soup.
column9: A verb for putting food into a bowl or plate: 盛飯, 盛湯, 盛一碗. The other reading, shèng, means flourishing.

column3: Mostly a bound character that joins another: 盛开 (bloom), 盛行 (be popular), 盛大 (grand), 繁盛 and 旺盛 (thriving, vigorous). The same character is read chéng when it means to hold or ladle out food.
column4: 春天，公园里百花盛开。
column5: 春天，公園裡百花盛開。
column6: Chūntiān, gōngyuán lǐ bǎihuā shèng kāi.
column7: In spring the flowers bloom in profusion in the park.
column9: Mostly a bound character that joins another: 盛開 (bloom), 盛行 (be popular), 盛大 (grand), 繁盛 and 旺盛 (thriving, vigorous). The same character is read chéng when it means to hold or ladle out food.

column3: Both a verb and a noun: parents, teachers or the law 惩罚 someone, and the person 受到惩罚 or 接受惩罚. Often for a deliberate penalty meant to teach a lesson.
column4: 做错事就要受到惩罚。
column5: 做錯事就要受到懲罰。
column6: Zuò cuò shì jiù yào shòudào chéngfá.
column7: If you do wrong, you have to be punished.
column9: Both a verb and a noun: parents, teachers or the law 懲罰 someone, and the person 受到懲罰 or 接受懲罰. Often for a deliberate penalty meant to teach a lesson.

column3: Most often figurative: to set the record straight, as in 澄清事实, 澄清误会, 澄清谣言, typically in a statement or an interview. The literal sense is clear, limpid water. When liquid settles and becomes clear, 澄 is read dèng.
column4: 公司发表声明，澄清了这个误会。
column5: 公司發表聲明，澄清了這個誤會。
column6: Gōngsī fābiǎo shēngmíng, chéngqīng le zhège wùhuì.
column7: The company issued a statement clearing up the misunderstanding.
column9: Most often figurative: to set the record straight, as in 澄清事實, 澄清誤會, 澄清謠言, typically in a statement or an interview. The literal sense is clear, limpid water. When liquid settles and becomes clear, 澄 is read dèng.

column3: On its own it is mostly a color word, 橙色, or part of 橙汁. For the fruit, the mainland says 橙子 and Taiwan usually 柳丁 or 柳橙.
column4: 这件衣服是橙色的。
column5: 這件衣服是橙色的。
column6: Zhè jiàn yīfu shì chéng sè de.
column7: This piece of clothing is orange.
column9: On its own it is mostly a color word, 橙色, or part of 橙汁. For the fruit, the mainland says 橙子 and Taiwan usually 柳丁 or 柳橙.

column3: The scale for weighing, from market steelyards to kitchen scales; the measure word is 把 or 杆. Figuratively, 心里有杆秤 means having a sense of what is fair.
column4: 请用秤称一下这些苹果。
column5: 請用秤稱一下這些蘋果。
column6: Qǐng yòng chèng chēng yīxià zhèxiē píngguǒ.
column7: Please weigh these apples on the scale.
column9: The scale for weighing, from market steelyards to kitchen scales; the measure word is 把 or 杆. Figuratively, 心裡有桿秤 means having a sense of what is fair.

column3: A verb-object phrase, a trait praised in people: 能吃苦, 不怕吃苦, 吃得了苦, and the set phrase 吃苦耐劳 (hardworking and able to endure hardship). 吃 also means to suffer, which is why you "eat" hardship.
column4: 年轻人要不怕吃苦。
column5: 年輕人要不怕吃苦。
column6: Niánqīngrén yào bù pà chīkǔ.
column7: Young people should not be afraid of hardship.
column9: A verb-object phrase, a trait praised in people: 能吃苦, 不怕吃苦, 吃得了苦, and the set phrase 吃苦耐勞 (hardworking and able to endure hardship). 吃 also means to suffer, which is why you "eat" hardship.

column3: Said of a person's mind or senses, mildly negative: 反应迟钝 (slow to react), 感觉迟钝 (dulled senses), 头脑迟钝. For slow progress or development, 迟缓 fits better.
column4: 他的反应有点迟钝。
column5: 他的反應有點遲鈍。
column6: Tā de fǎnyìng yǒudiǎn chídùn.
column7: His reactions are a bit slow.
column9: Said of a person's mind or senses, mildly negative: 反應遲鈍 (slow to react), 感覺遲鈍 (dulled senses), 頭腦遲鈍. For slow progress or development, 遲緩 fits better.

column3: Describes slow movement, development or progress, a little formal: 行动迟缓, 进展迟缓, 发展迟缓. A slow mind or reaction is 迟钝 instead.
column4: 经济的发展很迟缓。
column5: 經濟的發展很遲緩。
column6: Jīngjì de fāzhǎn hěn chíhuǎn.
column7: Economic development is slow.
column9: Describes slow movement, development or progress, a little formal: 行動遲緩, 進展遲緩, 發展遲緩. A slow mind or reaction is 遲鈍 instead.

column3: To pause before acting or answering, common in narration: 迟疑了一下, 毫不迟疑 (without hesitation), 迟疑不决 (undecided). 疑 began as a picture of a man with a cane looking around with his mouth open, not knowing where to go.
column4: 她迟疑了很久，才点头答应。
column5: 她遲疑了很久，才點頭答應。
column6: Tā chíyí le hěn jiǔ, cái diǎntóu dāying.
column7: She hesitated for a long time before nodding yes.
column9: To pause before acting or answering, common in narration: 遲疑了一下, 毫不遲疑 (without hesitation), 遲疑不決 (undecided). 疑 began as a picture of a man with a cane looking around with his mouth open, not knowing where to go.

column3: Goes before a noun or follows 很: 持久战 (a protracted war), 持久的和平, 效果持久, 香味持久. It describes what keeps its effect over time.
column4: 这种香水的香味很持久。
column5: 這種香水的香味很持久。
column6: Zhè zhǒng xiāngshuǐ de xiāngwèi hěn chíjiǔ.
column7: This perfume has a very lasting scent.
column9: Goes before a noun or follows 很: 持久戰 (a protracted war), 持久的和平, 效果持久, 香味持久. It describes what keeps its effect over time.

column3: A geography word. It builds 赤道地区 (equatorial regions) and the country name 赤道几内亚 (Equatorial Guinea).
column4: 赤道附近的气候终年炎热。
column5: 赤道附近的氣候終年炎熱。
column6: Chìdào fùjìn de qìhòu zhōngnián yánrè.
column7: The climate near the equator is hot all year round.
column9: A geography word. It builds 赤道地區 (equatorial regions) and the country name 赤道幾內亞 (Equatorial Guinea).

column3: The usual partners are 财政 and 贸易: 财政赤字, 贸易赤字. Verbs are 出现 and 弥补 (to make up); the opposite is 盈余 (surplus).
column4: 政府今年的财政赤字很大。
column5: 政府今年的財政赤字很大。
column6: Zhèngfǔ jīnnián de cáizhèng chìzì hěn dà.
column7: The government's budget deficit is large this year.
column9: The usual partners are 財政 and 貿易: 財政赤字, 貿易赤字. Verbs are 出現 and 彌補 (to make up); the opposite is 盈餘 (surplus).

column3: It is followed by the role taken on, often a temporary or stand-in one: 充当翻译, 充当桥梁. A thing can do it too: a box can 充当 a table.
column4: 他临时充当我们的翻译。
column5: 他臨時充當我們的翻譯。
column6: Tā línshí chōngdāng wǒmen de fānyì.
column7: He acted as our interpreter for the time being.
column9: It is followed by the role taken on, often a temporary or stand-in one: 充當翻譯, 充當橋梁. A thing can do it too: a box can 充當 a table.

column3: It describes something abundant and flowing, mostly energy or nature: 精力充沛, 体力充沛, 雨量充沛, 阳光充沛. For a plain count of things, such as people or books, it is not used.
column4: 他每天都精力充沛。
column5: 他每天都精力充沛。
column6: Tā měitiān dōu jīnglì chōngpèi.
column7: He is full of energy every day.
column9: It describes something abundant and flowing, mostly energy or nature: 精力充沛, 體力充沛, 雨量充沛, 陽光充沛. For a plain count of things, such as people or books, it is not used.

column3: It is used for things that overlap: schedules, areas, duties, shapes. In grammar it also names reduplication, as in 看看 and 散散步. 重 is read chóng here, meaning to repeat, and zhòng when it means heavy.
column4: 两个会议的时间重叠了。
column5: 兩個會議的時間重疊了。
column6: Liǎng ge huìyì de shíjiān chóngdié le.
column7: The times of the two meetings overlap.
column9: It is used for things that overlap: schedules, areas, duties, shapes. In grammar it also names reduplication, as in 看看 and 散散步. 重 is read chóng here, meaning to repeat, and zhòng when it means heavy.

column3: It is a strong, formal word for admiration felt toward someone great: a hero, a scholar, a teacher of long standing. It is stronger and loftier than 尊敬 and is not said of an ordinary boss or acquaintance. Often 对…充满崇敬.
column4: 我们都很崇敬这位老科学家。
column5: 我們都很崇敬這位老科學家。
column6: Wǒmen dōu hěn chóngjìng zhè wèi lǎo kēxuéjiā.
column7: We all deeply revere this old scientist.
column9: It is a strong, formal word for admiration felt toward someone great: a hero, a scholar, a teacher of long standing. It is stronger and loftier than 尊敬 and is not said of an ordinary boss or acquaintance. Often 對…充滿崇敬.

column3: It is for things packed closely together: 人口稠密, 住户稠密, 稠密的居民区. It does not describe thick liquids; for porridge or soup that is thick, use 稠 alone (粥很稠).
column4: 这个地区人口稠密。
column5: 這個地區人口稠密。
column6: Zhège dìqū rénkǒu chóumì.
column7: This area is densely populated.
column9: It is for things packed closely together: 人口稠密, 住戶稠密, 稠密的居民區. It does not describe thick liquids; for porridge or soup that is thick, use 稠 alone (粥很稠).

column3: It is for organizing something big ahead of time, such as an event, a wedding, a shop opening or a committee: 筹备婚礼, 筹备工作, 筹备委员会. It is both verb and noun; 筹备中 means "in preparation". The 筹 also means to raise money, as in 筹款.
column4: 我们正在筹备明年的展览。
column5: 我們正在籌備明年的展覽。
column6: Wǒmen zhèngzài chóubèi míngnián de zhǎnlǎn.
column7: We are preparing next year's exhibition.
column9: It is for organizing something big ahead of time, such as an event, a wedding, a shop opening or a committee: 籌備婚禮, 籌備工作, 籌備委員會. It is both verb and noun; 籌備中 means "in preparation". The 籌 also means to raise money, as in 籌款.

column3: It is about what is morally ugly, not what looks plain: 丑恶的嘴脸, 丑恶的行为, 丑恶现象. For a face or a coat that is simply unattractive, say 难看. 恶 is è here, meaning evil, but wù when it means to hate, as in 厌恶.
column4: 他的丑恶行为终于被揭露了。
column5: 他的醜惡行為終於被揭露了。
column6: Tā de chǒu'è xíngwéi zhōngyú bèi jiēlù le.
column7: His vile conduct was finally exposed.
column9: It is about what is morally ugly, not what looks plain: 醜惡的嘴臉, 醜惡的行為, 醜惡現象. For a face or a coat that is simply unattractive, say 難看. 惡 is è here, meaning evil, but wù when it means to hate, as in 厭惡.

column3: Mostly it means to betray: 出卖朋友, 出卖国家, 出卖秘密, 出卖灵魂. For ordinary selling in speech, say 卖; 出卖 for goods sounds formal or like an old notice.
column4: 他为了钱出卖了自己的朋友。
column5: 他為了錢出賣了自己的朋友。
column6: Tā wèile qián chūmài le zìjǐ de péngyou.
column7: He betrayed his own friend for money.
column9: Mostly it means to betray: 出賣朋友, 出賣國家, 出賣秘密, 出賣靈魂. For ordinary selling in speech, say 賣; 出賣 for goods sounds formal or like an old notice.

column3: It describes being so absorbed that you are lost to the world, whether in thought or in something enjoyable. It usually follows a verb with 得 (看得出神, 听得出神) or takes 了 (看出了神).
column4: 孩子们听故事听得出神。
column5: 孩子們聽故事聽得出神。
column6: Háizimen tīng gùshi tīng de chūshén.
column7: The children listened to the story, completely absorbed.
column9: It describes being so absorbed that you are lost to the world, whether in thought or in something enjoyable. It usually follows a verb with 得 (看得出神, 聽得出神) or takes 了 (看出了神).

column3: It is nearly always said of a person's future promise, mostly in 有出息 (will make something of themselves) and 没出息 (a scolding for someone with no ambition or drive). Parents and elders say it about children and young people.
column4: 他儿子很有出息，在大学当教授。
column5: 他兒子很有出息，在大學當教授。
column6: Tā érzi hěn yǒu chūxi, zài dàxué dāng jiàoshòu.
column7: His son has done well for himself and is a university professor.
column9: It is nearly always said of a person's future promise, mostly in 有出息 (will make something of themselves) and 沒出息 (a scolding for someone with no ambition or drive). Parents and elders say it about children and young people.

column3: It is the circumstances a person is in, usually hard ones: 处境困难, 处境危险, 处境尴尬. It goes with a person (他的处境), and 了解 or 同情 someone's 处境 is a common phrase. 处 is read chǔ here, meaning to be in a position, and chù when it means a place.
column4: 他的处境越来越困难。
column5: 他的處境越來越困難。
column6: Tā de chǔjìng yuèláiyuè kùnnan.
column7: His situation is getting harder and harder.
column9: It is the circumstances a person is in, usually hard ones: 處境困難, 處境危險, 處境尷尬. It goes with a person (他的處境), and 了解 or 同情 someone's 處境 is a common phrase. 處 is read chǔ here, meaning to be in a position, and chù when it means a place.

column3: It is a formal word for dealing with an incident, a case or a person, used by authorities and in reports: 妥善处置, 处置不当, 依法处置. It sounds more official than 处理 and can mean punishing.
column4: 警方已经妥善处置了这起事故。
column5: 警方已經妥善處置了這起事故。
column6: Jǐngfāng yǐjīng tuǒshàn chǔzhì le zhè qǐ shìgù.
column7: The police have already handled the accident properly.
column9: It is a formal word for dealing with an incident, a case or a person, used by authorities and in reports: 妥善處置, 處置不當, 依法處置. It sounds more official than 處理 and can mean punishing.

column3: It is both verb and noun, for stock kept for future need, often on a large scale: 外汇储备, 粮食储备, 人才储备, 知识储备. For ordinary saving at home, say 存. Taiwan reads 储 as chú.
column4: 国家储备了大量粮食。
column5: 國家儲備了大量糧食。
column6: Guójiā chǔbèi le dàliàng liángshi.
column7: The country has stockpiled a large amount of grain.
column9: It is both verb and noun, for stock kept for future need, often on a large scale: 外匯儲備, 糧食儲備, 人才儲備, 知識儲備. For ordinary saving at home, say 存. Taiwan reads 儲 as chú.

column3: It is a formal word for breaking a law, a rule or a taboo, or for crossing someone's dignity: 触犯法律, 触犯规定, 触犯众怒. For offending a person in daily life, 得罪 is the usual word.
column4: 这样做会触犯法律。
column5: 這樣做會觸犯法律。
column6: Zhèyàng zuò huì chùfàn fǎlǜ.
column7: Doing it this way would break the law.
column9: It is a formal word for breaking a law, a rule or a taboo, or for crossing someone's dignity: 觸犯法律, 觸犯規定, 觸犯眾怒. For offending a person in daily life, 得罪 is the usual word.

column3: It is a written, descriptive idiom, and in practice it is about traffic and crowds, not rivers: 车辆川流不息, 行人川流不息. It paints a busy, unbroken scene. Taiwan reads the last syllable xí: 川流不息 is chuān liú bù xí there.
column4: 街上的车辆川流不息。
column5: 街上的車輛川流不息。
column6: Jiē shàng de chēliàng chuānliúbùxī.
column7: Cars stream along the street without stopping.
column9: It is a written, descriptive idiom, and in practice it is about traffic and crowds, not rivers: 車輛川流不息, 行人川流不息. It paints a busy, unbroken scene. Taiwan reads the last syllable xí: 川流不息 is chuān liú bù xí there.

column3: It is a fairly formal verb that goes with the space you pass through: a tunnel, a desert, a city, a border. It is also the name of the time-travel story genre: 穿越小说, 穿越剧.
column4: 火车穿越了长长的隧道。
column5: 火車穿越了長長的隧道。
column6: Huǒchē chuānyuè le chángcháng de suìdào.
column7: The train passed through a long tunnel.
column9: It is a fairly formal verb that goes with the space you pass through: a tunnel, a desert, a city, a border. It is also the name of the time-travel story genre: 穿越小說, 穿越劇.

column3: It is for passing on skills, knowledge or experience from someone who has mastered them, such as a master, an elder or an expert: 传授技艺, 传授经验. For teaching a class, 教 is the everyday word. 传 is read chuán here, meaning to pass on, but zhuàn when it means a biography.
column4: 老师傅把手艺传授给了徒弟。
column5: 老師傅把手藝傳授給了徒弟。
column6: Lǎo shīfu bǎ shǒuyì chuánshòu gěi le túdi.
column7: The old master passed his craft on to his apprentice.
column9: It is for passing on skills, knowledge or experience from someone who has mastered them, such as a master, an elder or an expert: 傳授技藝, 傳授經驗. For teaching a class, 教 is the everyday word. 傳 is read chuán here, meaning to pass on, but zhuàn when it means a biography.

column3: It is a formal collective word for ships and boats of every kind, seen in port notices, shipping law and news reports. In everyday speech people just say 船.
column4: 港口有很多船舶进出。
column5: 港口有很多船舶進出。
column6: Gǎngkǒu yǒu hěn duō chuánbó jìnchū.
column7: Many ships come and go at the port.
column9: It is a formal collective word for ships and boats of every kind, seen in port notices, shipping law and news reports. In everyday speech people just say 船.

column3: It splits like a verb and its object: 喘口气, 喘了一口气. 喘口气 is also the usual way to say take a short break from busy work, and 喘不过气来 describes being unable to breathe or being overwhelmed.
column4: 他跑得太快，停下来直喘气。
column5: 他跑得太快，停下來直喘氣。
column6: Tā pǎo de tài kuài, tíng xiàlái zhí chuǎnqì.
column7: He ran so fast that he stopped and gasped for breath.
column9: It splits like a verb and its object: 喘口氣, 喘了一口氣. 喘口氣 is also the usual way to say take a short break from busy work, and 喘不過氣來 describes being unable to breathe or being overwhelmed.

column3: It is everyday and informal: to claim more than is true, so a friend may say 你别吹牛了. The fuller 吹牛皮 means the same. It splits like a verb and its object (吹了牛, 吹什么牛).
column4: 他总爱吹牛，说自己会五种语言。
column5: 他總愛吹牛，說自己會五種語言。
column6: Tā zǒng ài chuīniú, shuō zìjǐ huì wǔ zhǒng yǔyán.
column7: He is always bragging that he speaks five languages.
column9: It is everyday and informal: to claim more than is true, so a friend may say 你別吹牛了. The fuller 吹牛皮 means the same. It splits like a verb and its object (吹了牛, 吹什麼牛).

column3: It is critical in tone: praise that is excessive or insincere, usually to win favor. It takes a person as its object (吹捧上司) and often appears as 互相吹捧.
column4: 他们互相吹捧，谁也不批评谁。
column5: 他們互相吹捧，誰也不批評誰。
column6: Tāmen hùxiāng chuīpěng, shéi yě bù pīpíng shéi.
column7: They flatter each other and nobody criticizes anybody.
column9: It is critical in tone: praise that is excessive or insincere, usually to win favor. It takes a person as its object (吹捧上司) and often appears as 互相吹捧.

column3: It is a picturesque, slightly nostalgic word for the smoke of a village at mealtime: 炊烟袅袅, 缕缕炊烟. It evokes home and the countryside more than an actual chimney. 炊 takes its sound from 吹, which fits blowing on a fire to get it going.
column4: 村子上空飘着缕缕炊烟。
column5: 村子上空飄著縷縷炊煙。
column6: Cūnzi shàngkōng piāozhe lǚlǚ chuīyān.
column7: Wisps of cooking smoke drift above the village.
column9: It is a picturesque, slightly nostalgic word for the smoke of a village at mealtime: 炊煙裊裊, 縷縷炊煙. It evokes home and the countryside more than an actual chimney. 炊 takes its sound from 吹, which fits blowing on a fire to get it going.

column3: In math and building, 垂直于 says what a line or wall is perpendicular to (垂直于地面), and the other direction is 水平. It is also used for anything straight up and down, like a cliff or a drop: 垂直的峭壁. 垂 began as a picture of flowers hanging from a plant.
column4: 旗杆和地面垂直。
column5: 旗桿和地面垂直。
column6: Qígān hé dìmiàn chuízhí.
column7: The flagpole is perpendicular to the ground.
column9: In math and building, 垂直於 says what a line or wall is perpendicular to (垂直於地面), and the other direction is 水平. It is also used for anything straight up and down, like a cliff or a drop: 垂直的峭壁. 垂 began as a picture of flowers hanging from a plant.

column3: On its own it is rare, and the everyday hammer is 锤子 (铁锤 for a heavy iron one). As a verb it means to hammer, as in 千锤百炼 (tempered by a thousand blows); thumping someone's back is 捶背, with 捶.
column4: 他用锤子把钉子敲进墙里。
column5: 他用錘子把釘子敲進牆裡。
column6: Tā yòng chuí zi bǎ dīngzi qiāo jìn qiáng lǐ.
column7: He drove the nail into the wall with a hammer.
column9: On its own it is rare, and the everyday hammer is 錘子 (鐵錘 for a heavy iron one). As a verb it means to hammer, as in 千錘百鍊 (tempered by a thousand blows); thumping someone's back is 捶背, with 捶.

column3: It is abstract: motives, reasons, luck, a style or a feeling. It often sits before 是 to say it is nothing but that: 纯粹是误会, 纯粹是运气. For pure water or gold, use 纯 alone (纯金).
column4: 这纯粹是个误会。
column5: 這純粹是個誤會。
column6: Zhè chúncuì shì ge wùhuì.
column7: This is purely a misunderstanding.
column9: It is abstract: motives, reasons, luck, a style or a feeling. It often sits before 是 to say it is nothing but that: 純粹是誤會, 純粹是運氣. For pure water or gold, use 純 alone (純金).
